levels.title: Mathematical & Computational Foundations
levels.scope: master the core mathematical disciplines and numerical computing paradigms required for modern AI research: linear algebra, multivariable calculus, probability theory, information theory, and tensor automatic differentiation.

modules.name: Linear Algebra & Vector Spaces

objectives.text: Understand vector spaces, subspaces, linear independence, basis, dimension, and linear transformations from geometric and algebraic viewpoints.
Master matrix operations, rank-nullity theorem, invertibility, determinants, and matrix inverses in computational and theoretical contexts.
Analyze eigenvalues, eigenvectors, characteristic polynomials, and geometric versus algebraic multiplicity.
Understand spectral decomposition, symmetric matrices, positive semi-definite (PSD) matrices, and quadratic forms.
Master Singular Value Decomposition (SVD): compact SVD, thin SVD, truncated SVD, low-rank matrix approximation, and the Eckart-Young-Mirsky theorem.
Understand vector norms (L1, L2, Lp, L-infinity) and matrix norms (Frobenius, spectral norm, nuclear norm) and their roles in regularization.
Compute inner products, projections, orthogonal complements, and Gram-Schmidt orthogonalization.
Explore condition numbers, ill-conditioned linear systems, matrix pseudo-inverses (Moore-Penrose), and numerical stability in high dimensions.

modules.outcome: derive SVD decompositions, prove spectral properties of symmetric positive semi-definite matrices, and analyze high-dimensional linear mappings algebraically and geometrically.

modules.name: Multivariable Calculus & Automatic Differentiation

objectives.text: Compute partial derivatives, directional derivatives, gradients, Jacobian matrices, and Hessian matrices for scalar and vector-valued multivariable functions.
Understand multivariate Taylor series expansions, quadratic approximations, and critical points (local minima, maxima, saddle points).
Master the multivariate chain rule across nested vector-to-vector and matrix-to-matrix mappings.
Derive backpropagation mathematically as a reverse-mode automatic differentiation algorithm over computational directed acyclic graphs (DAGs).
Contrast forward-mode automatic differentiation (dual numbers) and reverse-mode automatic differentiation in terms of computational and memory complexity.
Analyze matrix and tensor calculus: computing derivatives with respect to vectors, matrices, and multi-dimensional tensors using index notation and Einstein summation.
Understand higher-order gradients: Hessian-vector products (HVPs), Fisher Information Matrix, and their applications in second-order optimization.

modules.outcome: implement analytical tensor backpropagation manually on paper and verify gradients against numerical finite differences.

modules.name: Probability Theory & Stochastic Foundations

objectives.text: Understand probability spaces, sigma-algebras, random variables, cumulative distribution functions, and probability density functions.
Analyze discrete distributions (Bernoulli, Binomial, Categorical, Poisson) and continuous distributions (Gaussian, Multivariate Normal, Uniform, Beta, Dirichlet).
Master joint distributions, conditional distributions, marginalization, Bayes' theorem, independence, and conditional independence.
Derive expectations, variances, covariances, correlation coefficients, covariance matrices, and moments of multidimensional distributions.
Understand change of variables formula for continuous probability density functions, Jacobians of transformations, and normalizing flows foundations.
Analyze law of large numbers (weak and strong), central limit theorem, and concentration inequalities (Markov, Chebyshev, Hoeffding, Chernoff bounds).
Understand maximum likelihood estimation (MLE), maximum a posteriori (MAP) estimation, and their exact relations to loss functions in supervised learning.

modules.outcome: manipulate multivariate Gaussian densities, derive MLE and MAP estimators analytically, and bound sample estimate deviations using concentration inequalities.

modules.name: Information Theory & Entropy

objectives.text: Define Shannon entropy as a measure of uncertainty and surprise for discrete and continuous (differential entropy) random variables.
Compute joint entropy, conditional entropy, and derive the chain rule of entropy.
Master Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence (relative entropy): mathematical definition, non-negativity (Gibbs' inequality), asymmetry, and directionality (forward KL vs reverse KL).
Understand cross-entropy loss, its relationship to Shannon entropy and KL divergence, and why it forms the standard surrogate loss in classification.
Analyze mutual information, channel capacity, data processing inequality, and the information bottleneck principle in deep neural representations.
Understand Wasserstein distance (Earth Mover's Distance) and optimal transport fundamentals versus f-divergences in probability distribution alignment.

modules.outcome: prove Gibbs' inequality, compute analytical KL divergence between multivariate Gaussians, and contrast forward and reverse KL behavior on multi-modal targets.

modules.name: Numerical Scientific Computing & JAX/PyTorch Internals

objectives.text: Understand floating-point representation (IEEE 754: FP64, FP32, FP16, BF16, FP8), precision limits, machine epsilon, underflow, and overflow.
Master numerically stable computation: log-sum-exp trick for Softmax, log-domain probabilities, and mitigating vanishing gradients.
Implement vectorized and tensorized mathematical operations using NumPy, PyTorch, and JAX with zero Python-level loops.
Understand computation graphs, tensor strides, views, contiguous memory layout, broadcasting rules, and inplace mutations.
Master JAX functional programming primitives: pure functions, jit (XLA compilation), vmap (vectorized batching), and grad (algorithmic differentiation).
Profile floating point operations (FLOPs), memory bandwidth, CPU-GPU data transfers, and tensor allocation bottlenecks.

modules.outcome: write high-performance vectorized numerical code in PyTorch/JAX that runs stably in low-precision floating-point regimes without numerical underflow.

modules.name: Capstone: Build an Autograd Engine from Mathematical First Principles

objectives.text: Build a complete tensor-valued reverse-mode automatic differentiation engine from scratch in pure Python and NumPy with no deep learning frameworks.
Implement a computational Tensor class supporting dynamic DAG graph construction, topological sorting, and reverse topological gradient accumulation.
Implement forward and backward passes for fundamental mathematical operations: addition, subtraction, multiplication, matrix multiplication, transpose, power, log, and exp.
Implement multi-dimensional tensor broadcasting mechanics and ensure gradient reduction over broadcasted dimensions during backward execution.
Implement activation functions with numerical stability guards: Sigmoid, ReLU, GELU, and numerically stable Softmax with LogSumExp.
Implement loss functions: Mean Squared Error, Binary Cross Entropy, and Categorical Cross Entropy with one-hot targets.
Verify gradient correctness for every single primitive operation using numerical gradient checking (finite difference approximations) with a tolerance under 1e-5.
Construct and train a multi-layer perceptron (MLP) on a non-linear dataset using purely your custom autograd engine and SGD optimizer.
Document the exact mathematical Jacobian-vector products for each operator and analyze computational complexity of forward versus backward graph passes.

modules.finalResult: a verified, documented tensor autograd engine written from first principles that executes arbitrary mathematical computation graphs and trains neural networks.

completionOutcomes: Solve multivariable linear algebra systems and derive singular value decompositions analytically.
Analyze symmetric positive semi-definite matrices and compute spectral projections.
Derive the multivariate chain rule across tensor mappings using index notation.
Explain forward-mode versus reverse-mode automatic differentiation computational complexity.
Calculate gradients, Jacobians, and Hessians of multivariable scalar and vector functions.
Formulate loss functions as maximum likelihood or maximum a posteriori estimation problems.
Calculate Shannon entropy, joint entropy, conditional entropy, and mutual information.
Prove the non-negativity of Kullback-Leibler divergence and analyze mode-covering versus mode-seeking behavior.
Explain the mathematical difference between KL divergence and Wasserstein distance.
Handle floating-point precision issues and implement numerically stable operations like LogSumExp.
Write vectorized and memory-contiguous tensor transformations in PyTorch and JAX.
Use JAX functional primitives including pure functions, grad, vmap, and jit compilation.
Construct a dynamic computational directed acyclic graph and perform topological sorting.
Accumulate multivariable gradients backward through complex computational trees.
Implement tensor broadcasting gradient reduction correctly in custom autograd passes.
Derive analytical gradients for matrix multiplication and multi-layer neural network parameters.
Verify empirical gradients against mathematical derivatives using finite differences.
Read theoretical machine learning research papers containing rigorous linear algebra and probability proofs.
Progression: Linear Algebra → Multivariable Calculus → Probability Theory → Information Theory → Numerical Computing → Custom Autograd Engine.

levels.title: Statistical Learning Theory & Classical ML
levels.scope: explore the theoretical foundations of statistical learning: PAC learning, empirical risk minimization, VC dimension, generalization bounds, convex optimization, kernel methods, and probabilistic graphical models.

modules.name: The Learning Problem & Empirical Risk Minimization

objectives.text: Formulate the statistical learning problem: input space, output space, unknown data-generating distribution P(X, Y), hypothesis class H, and loss functions.
Define true risk (expected loss) versus empirical risk (training loss) and formulate the Empirical Risk Minimization (ERM) principle.
Analyze the inductive bias of hypothesis classes and explain why unconstrained learning without inductive bias is mathematically impossible.
Decompose expected generalization error into approximation error, estimation error, and irreducible optimization error.
Understand the classical bias-variance decomposition for mean squared error: bias squared, variance, and noise terms.
Analyze overfitting and underfitting from statistical learning perspectives and study the effect of sample size N on generalization error.
Examine surrogate loss functions: 0-1 loss intractability, convex surrogates (hinge loss, logistic loss, exponential loss), and classification calibration.

modules.outcome: formulate machine learning problems rigorously in the language of statistical decision theory and analyze risk decomposition.

modules.name: PAC Learning & Generalization Bounds

objectives.text: Master Probably Approximately Correct (PAC) learning framework: epsilon-accuracy, delta-confidence, sample complexity, and computational complexity.
Prove finite hypothesis class generalization bounds using Hoeffding's inequality and the union bound for realizable and agnostic settings.
Understand uniform convergence: bounding the supremum of empirical risk deviations over the entire hypothesis class.
Define Rademacher complexity and Gaussian complexity as data-dependent measures of hypothesis class richness.
Study growth functions, Shattering, and Vapnik-Chervonenkis (VC) dimension for infinite hypothesis classes.
Prove Sauer-Shelah lemma and derive VC dimension bounds for linear classifiers, hyperplanes, and polynomial classifiers.
Understand modern generalization frontiers: PAC-Bayes bounds, margin bounds, and where classical uniform convergence bounds fail in deep learning.

modules.outcome: compute VC dimensions for geometric hypothesis classes and derive formal sample complexity bounds for PAC learnability.

modules.name: Convex Optimization & Duality Theory

objectives.text: Understand convex sets, convex functions, epigraphs, subgradients, and subdifferentials for non-smooth convex objectives.
Master optimality conditions: Fermat's rule for unconstrained problems, Karush-Kuhn-Tucker (KKT) conditions for constrained optimization.
Formulate Lagrangian functions, primal optimization problems, Lagrange dual functions, and dual optimization problems.
Understand weak duality, strong duality, Slater's constraint qualification condition, and zero duality gap.
Analyze first-order optimization methods: gradient descent, projected gradient descent, subgradient descent, and convergence rates for convex and strongly convex functions.
Analyze accelerated first-order algorithms: Polyak's heavy-ball method, Nesterov accelerated gradient, and optimal O(1/k^2) convergence rates.
Explore second-order methods: Newton's method, Quasi-Newton methods (BFGS, L-BFGS), and trust-region algorithms with quadratic convergence properties.

modules.outcome: derive dual optimization problems analytically, verify KKT conditions, and analyze algorithmic convergence rates mathematically.

modules.name: Kernel Methods & Non-Parametric Theory

objectives.text: Formulate linear models for regression and classification: ordinary least squares, ridge regression, and Lasso with L1 sparsity proofs.
Understand reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces (RKHS), the Moore-Aronszajn theorem, and Mercer's theorem for positive definite kernels.
Master the kernel trick: mapping data implicitly into infinite-dimensional feature spaces via kernel evaluation k(x, x').
Analyze canonical kernels: polynomial kernels, Gaussian Radial Basis Function (RBF) kernel, Laplacian kernel, and neural tangent kernels (NTK) introduction.
Derive Support Vector Machines (SVM) primal and dual formulations, support vectors geometry, slack variables, and soft-margin formulations.
Formulate Kernel Ridge Regression and Gaussian Processes: covariance functions, posterior Gaussian distributions, and Bayesian non-parametrics.
Understand non-parametric estimation: k-nearest neighbors convergence rates, Nadaraya-Watson kernel regression, and the curse of dimensionality.

modules.outcome: prove Mercer's conditions for custom kernels, derive the dual SVM optimization problem, and implement Gaussian Process regression with analytical posteriors.

modules.name: Probabilistic Graphical Models & Approximate Inference

objectives.text: Understand Directed A Graphical Models (Bayesian Networks): factorization of joint distributions, d-separation, and conditional independence properties.
Understand Undirected Graphical Models (Markov Random Fields): cliques, potential functions, Gibbs distributions, and the Hammersley-Clifford theorem.
Formulate exact inference algorithms: variable elimination, belief propagation on trees, and the sum-product / max-product junction tree algorithm.
Analyze the computational complexity of exact inference and explain why general inference is NP-hard.
Master approximate inference through sampling: Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC), Metropolis-Hastings algorithm, and Gibbs sampling.
Master approximate inference through variational methods: Variational Inference (VI), Evidence Lower Bound (ELBO), mean-field approximation, and coordinate ascent variational inference (CAVI).
Explore the Expectation-Maximization (EM) algorithm: Jensen's inequality derivation, Gaussian Mixture Models (GMM), and convergence properties.

modules.outcome: derive the Evidence Lower Bound from Jensen's inequality and implement the Expectation-Maximization algorithm for latent Gaussian mixtures.

modules.name: Capstone: Empirical and Theoretical Study of Generalization in Kernel Regression

objectives.text: Formulate a rigorous research experiment comparing theoretical generalization bounds against empirical test error across varying sample sizes N and dimensions D.
Implement Kernel Ridge Regression and Support Vector Machines entirely from scratch using quadratic programming solvers (CVXPY/SciPy).
Derive the analytical generalization error bound using empirical Rademacher complexity and RKHS norm constraints.
Compute empirical Rademacher complexity via Monte Carlo sampling of random Rademacher variables over synthetically generated non-linear manifolds.
Investigate the role of regularization parameter lambda on eigenvalue decay of the kernel Gram matrix and the effective degrees of freedom.
Measure the gap between worst-case theoretical generalization bounds and actual empirical test risk across overparameterized versus underparameterized regimes.
Produce publication-quality research figures: risk curves, eigenvalue spectra, empirical vs theoretical bound gaps, and decision boundaries.
Write a formal academic report (ICML/NeurIPS formatting) analyzing where uniform convergence bounds remain tight and where they become vacuous.

modules.finalResult: a reproducible research benchmark and theoretical report validating kernel generalization bounds against empirical learning dynamics.

completionOutcomes: Formulate learning problems in the statistical decision theory framework.
Prove risk decomposition into bias, variance, and irreducible error.
Derive generalization error bounds for finite hypothesis classes using Hoeffding's inequality.
Define the PAC learning model and compute sample complexity for realizable hypotheses.
Calculate the VC dimension of linear classifiers and simple geometric families.
State and prove properties of convex functions, subgradients, and epigraphs.
Derive the Karush-Kuhn-Tucker (KKT) conditions for constrained optimization problems.
Formulate the Lagrangian dual problem and prove weak duality.
Explain Nesterov acceleration and prove its optimal convergence rate for smooth convex functions.
Prove that a given function is a valid Mercer kernel and construct an RKHS mapping.
Derive the dual formulation of Support Vector Machines and identify support vectors geometrically.
Implement Gaussian Process regression and compute closed-form analytical predictive posteriors.
Determine conditional independence in Bayesian networks using d-separation.
Derive the Evidence Lower Bound (ELBO) mathematically using Jensen's inequality.
Implement the Expectation-Maximization algorithm for latent variable models.
Compare MCMC sampling and variational inference for approximate posterior estimation.
Analyze why classical VC and Rademacher bounds can become vacuous in deep overparameterized models.
Conduct a rigorous theoretical and empirical comparison between theoretical bounds and empirical generalization.

Progression: Empirical Risk Minimization → PAC Bounds & VC Dimension → Convex Optimization & Duality → Kernel Methods & RKHS → Graphical Models & Variational Inference → Generalization Benchmark Study.

levels.title: Deep Learning Theory & Optimization Dynamics
levels.scope: examine the mathematical mechanics of deep neural networks: expressivity and universal approximation theorems, loss surface geometry, non-convex optimization dynamics, adaptive optimizers, normalization layers, and implicit regularization.

modules.name: Expressivity & Universal Approximation Theory

objectives.text: Study the Universal Approximation Theorem for single-hidden-layer networks: Cybenko's theorem for sigmoidal activations and Hornik's theorem for arbitrary continuous activations.
Analyze width versus depth trade-offs: exponential expressivity of deep architectures in separating complex topological manifolds.
Understand linear regions of deep ReLU networks: counting maximal numbers of linear regions as a function of depth, width, and input dimension.
Investigate the Neural Tangent Kernel (NTK) regime: infinite-width limits, linear dynamics in function space, and kernel convergence.
Analyze inductive bias of convolutional architectures: translation equivariance, weight sharing, locality, and sample complexity advantages on spatial data.
Examine expressivity limitations: parity problems, graph isomorphism testing limitations (Weisfeiler-Lehman hierarchy in GNNs), and depth lower bounds.

modules.outcome: derive proofs for single-layer universal approximation and compute exact bounds on linear regions created by deep ReLU feedforward networks.

modules.name: Loss Landscapes & Non-Convex Optimization

objectives.text: Analyze the geometry of deep learning loss surfaces: high dimensionality, non-convexity, saddle points, local minima, and plateaus.
Understand the strict saddle property and escaping saddle points via perturbed stochastic gradient descent (Ge et al.).
Study the landscape geometry of overparameterized networks: mode connectivity, linear mode connectivity, and loss valleys.
Analyze Hessian spectrum dynamics: dominant eigenvalues, bulk distribution, ill-conditioning, and edge of stability phenomenon.
Understand flat versus sharp minima: trace of the Hessian, spectral radius, Fisher information, and their empirical correlation with test generalization (Keskar et al., Dinh et al.).
Examine Sharpness-Aware Minimization (SAM): mathematical formulation, minimax perturbation objective, and regularizing loss curvature.
Investigate loss surface visualization techniques: filter-normalized random directions, 1D and 2D contour projections (Li et al.).

modules.outcome: compute the top eigenvalues of the empirical Hessian along training trajectories and measure loss landscape curvature across different architectural choices.

modules.name: Stochastic Optimization & Adaptive Learning Dynamics

objectives.text: Analyze Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD): unbiased gradient estimates, gradient variance, mini-batching dynamics, and convergence rates on non-convex objectives.
Study Polyak momentum and Nesterov accelerated gradient in stochastic regimes: dampening oscillations and traversing ravines.
Master adaptive learning rate algorithms: AdaGrad, RMSprop, Adam, and AdamW (Loshchilov & Hutter decoupled weight decay proof).
Analyze Adam's failure modes: non-convergence on simple convex objectives (Reddi et al. AMSGrad), hyperparameter sensitivity (beta1, beta2, epsilon), and heavy-tailed noise.
Investigate learning rate schedules: linear warmup, step decay, exponential decay, cosine annealing with warm restarts, and 1cycle policy.
Analyze the stochastic differential equation (SDE) view of SGD: Langevin dynamics, diffusion approximations, and escape from sharp local basins.
Examine gradient clipping: norm clipping vs value clipping, preserving gradient direction, and preventing catastrophic loss spikes during deep training.

modules.outcome: implement AdamW from scratch with decoupled L2 weight decay and prove that standard L2 regularization in Adam is mathematically non-equivalent to weight decay.

modules.name: Normalization & Signal Propagation Dynamics

objectives.text: Analyze the internal covariate shift hypothesis and alternative theoretical explanations of normalization effectiveness (Santurkar et al., loss smoothing).
Master Batch Normalization: mathematical formulation, training versus inference running statistics, scale-invariance, and gradient scaling properties.
Understand Layer Normalization: channel-wise normalization, invariance to shift and scaling, and suitability for sequential and autoregressive models.
Analyze RMSNorm (Root Mean Square Normalization): computational efficiency, removing mean centering, and mathematical properties in modern LLMs.
Study weight initialization theory: Xavier/Glorot initialization for symmetric activations, He/Kaiming initialization for ReLU/GELU, and preserving variance across layers.
Analyze dynamical isometry and signal propagation in deep networks: preventing exploding/vanishing gradients at initialization (Pennington et al.).
Examine alternatives to normalization: Fixup initialization, ReZero, and DeepNorm for extremely deep residual architectures.

modules.outcome: prove gradient variance preservation under Kaiming initialization and implement LayerNorm and RMSNorm with analytical backward pass derivations.

modules.name: Implicit Regularization & Double Descent

objectives.text: Understand the classical bias-variance trade-off versus modern deep learning observations: overparameterization without explicit regularization.
Analyze implicit regularization: how SGD selects minimum L2-norm solutions in underdetermined linear regression and maximum margin solutions in separable classification.
Study the Double Descent phenomenon (Belkin et al.): classical U-curve, interpolation threshold peak, and the overparameterized modern regime.
Differentiate model-wise double descent, sample-wise double descent, and epoch-wise double descent across training horizons.
Analyze explicit regularization techniques: L1 (Lasso) and L2 (Ridge/weight decay), Dropout (approximate variational inference interpretation), and data augmentation.
Examine label noise and memorization: early stopping, Arpit et al. study on networks learning patterns before memorizing noise, and clean-up phases.

modules.outcome: reproduce epoch-wise and model-size double descent empirically on controlled synthetic and benchmark datasets.

modules.name: Capstone: Empirical Investigation of Double Descent and Loss Landscape Curvature

objectives.text: Design an empirical research experiment investigating the relationship between model parameter capacity, loss curvature, and generalization error.
Train a family of deep neural networks varying systematically from underparameterized to heavily overparameterized regimes across controlled label noise levels.
Implement an efficient Power Iteration algorithm to compute the spectral radius (top eigenvalue lambda_max) and trace of the empirical Hessian without forming full N x N Hessian matrices.
Measure loss sharpness around converged solutions using filter-normalized random direction perturbations.
Track training loss, test loss, generalization error, and Hessian sharpness across training epochs to empirically observe double descent peaks.
Evaluate the mitigating effects of explicit regularization (weight decay, dropout) and optimization curvature smoothing (Sharpness-Aware Minimization) on double descent severity.
Generate publication-quality research figures: test error vs parameter count curves, Hessian eigenvalue trajectories, and 2D loss surface contour maps.
Draft an academic research paper reporting findings with rigorous ablation tables and theoretical discussion linking empirical observations to NTK theory.

modules.finalResult: a reproducible research experiment and empirical paper dissecting double descent dynamics and loss landscape geometry in deep networks.

completionOutcomes: State and prove the Universal Approximation Theorem for single-hidden-layer networks.
Quantify the maximum number of linear regions in deep ReLU architectures.
Explain the Neural Tangent Kernel (NTK) regime and its assumptions regarding network width.
Analyze non-convex loss surfaces and characterize saddle points, local minima, and plateaus.
Compute the dominant eigenvalues of the empirical Hessian using power iteration and Hessian-vector products.
Explain the difference between flat and sharp minima and their relationship to generalization.
Derive the AdamW update rules and explain why standard L2 penalty fails in adaptive optimizers.
Analyze the stochastic differential equation (SDE) approximation of stochastic gradient descent.
Derive the variance preservation condition for Kaiming (He) weight initialization.
Implement Layer Normalization and RMSNorm with full analytical backward gradients.
Explain how residual connections and normalization maintain dynamical isometry in deep networks.
Define implicit regularization and explain minimum-norm selection by gradient descent.
Formulate and empirically reproduce the double descent curve across model capacity and training epochs.
Implement Sharpness-Aware Minimization (SAM) and analyze its effect on Hessian spectra.
Visualize 2D loss surfaces using filter-normalized random perturbation directions.
Conduct controlled experiments measuring the effects of label noise and overparameterization on test risk.

Progression: Expressivity & Universal Approximation → Loss Landscapes & Hessian Geometry → Adaptive Optimization & AdamW → Normalization & Signal Propagation → Implicit Regularization & Double Descent → Landscape Curvature Capstone.

levels.title: Sequence Modeling & Transformer Architectures
levels.scope: explore sequence modeling theory from recurrent networks to modern Transformer architectures: self-attention mechanics, positional encodings, attention variants, hardware-aware algorithms, and sub-quadratic sequence models.

modules.name: Sequence Modeling Foundations & Attention Mechanics

objectives.text: Analyze autoregressive sequence modeling: conditional probability factorization via chain rule of probability, cross-entropy objective, and perplexity metric.
Review recurrent neural networks (RNNs), LSTMs, and GRUs: gating mechanisms, cell state dynamics, and vanishing/exploding gradients over long contexts.
Analyze the information bottleneck of fixed-length encoder-decoder representations in early neural machine translation (Cho et al., Sutskever et al.).
Understand the additive attention mechanism (Bahdanau et al.) and multiplicative attention (Luong et al.) as alignment models in latent space.
Contrast seq2seq with attention against recurrence: path length between distant tokens, parallelization capacity across time steps, and O(N) sequential complexity.

modules.outcome: derive gradients of recurrent cells versus attention mechanisms over time and explain the vanishing gradient bottleneck in RNNs.

modules.name: Mathematical Anatomy of the Transformer

objectives.text: Master Scaled Dot-Product Attention: queries Q, keys K, values V, scaling factor 1/sqrt(d_k), softmax normalization, and value weighted combination.
Explain why scaling by 1/sqrt(d_k) prevents large dot-product magnitudes from pushing the Softmax function into vanishing gradient saturation regions.
Analyze Multi-Head Attention (MHA): projection matrices, multi-subspace representation learning, concatenation, output projection, and parameter counts.
Derive the exact computational complexity and memory footprint of self-attention: O(N^2 * d) FLOPs and O(N^2) memory activation matrix for sequence length N.
Master Causal Masking: lower-triangular masking for autoregressive language modeling preventing information leakage from future tokens.
Analyze Transformer block architecture: Pre-LayerNorm (Pre-LN) versus Post-LayerNorm (Post-LN) stability dynamics (Xiong et al.), residual connections, and MLP/SwiGLU feedforward expansions.
Examine Multi-Query Attention (MQA) and Grouped-Query Attention (GQA): key-value head sharing, reducing KV cache bandwidth during inference, and quality trade-offs (Ainslie et al.).

modules.outcome: write modular, tensorized PyTorch code implementing Multi-Head Attention, Grouped-Query Attention, and Pre-LN Transformer blocks with causal masking from mathematical scratch.

modules.name: Positional Encodings & Context Length Generalization

objectives.text: Understand why self-attention is permutation-equivariant and requires explicit positional information to model sequence order.
Analyze Absolute Positional Encodings: sinusoidal functions (Vaswani et al.), wavelength frequencies, and learnable positional embedding tables.
Study Relative Positional Encodings: Shaw et al., Transformer-XL, and encoding relative displacement (i - j) between tokens rather than absolute indices.
Master Rotary Position Embedding (RoPE): complex number representation, 2D rotation matrices, inner product preservation, and frequency properties (Su et al.).
Analyze ALiBi (Attention with Linear Biases): decaying attention scores with linear query-key distance penalties, and zero-shot length extrapolation properties (Press et al.).
Investigate Context Window Extension techniques: Position Interpolation (Chen et al.), YaRN (Yet another RoPE extensioN method), and NTK-aware RoPE scaling.

modules.outcome: derive RoPE mathematically showing that the inner product of rotated queries and keys depends strictly on relative offset (m - n), and implement 2D tensor rotary rotation.

modules.name: Hardware-Aware Attention & Memory Efficiency

objectives.text: Understand GPU memory hierarchy: High Bandwidth Memory (HBM) versus on-chip SRAM, memory bandwidth vs compute throughput limits (roofline model).
Analyze the standard Softmax attention memory bottleneck: materializing the N x N attention matrix to HBM causes memory bandwidth saturation (IO bound).
Master FlashAttention (Dao et al.): tiling algorithm, computing Softmax incrementally using online softmax normalization (Milakov & Gimelshein), and never materializing N x N matrices in HBM.
Analyze FlashAttention backward pass: recomputing attention matrix in SRAM from queries, keys, and values instead of saving massive intermediate activation maps.
Study FlashAttention-2 and FlashAttention-3: work partitioning, reducing non-matmul FLOPs, warp-level parallelism, and asynchronous memory operations on Hopper architectures.
Examine KV Cache memory footprint during autoregressive generation: batch size, sequence length, layers, heads, dimension, and PagedAttention (vLLM) memory paging.

modules.outcome: derive the online Softmax algorithm mathematically and implement a tiled Softmax kernel demonstrating exact numerical equivalence without intermediate full-matrix storage.

modules.name: Sub-Quadratic Architectures & State Space Models

objectives.text: Analyze the fundamental scaling limit of dense Transformers: quadratic O(N^2) time and memory complexity restricting extreme context lengths.
Explore Linear Attention variants: kernel-based attention approximations, associative property of matrix multiplication, and O(N) complexity limits.
Study State Space Models (SSMs): continuous-time linear dynamical systems, discretization (bilinear/Euler transforms), and recurrent versus convolutional views (Gu et al., S4).
Master Mamba and Structured State Space Models (Gu & Dao): selective state spaces (S6), hardware-aware associative scan, input-dependent parameters, and linear-time scaling.
Compare Hybrid Architectures: combining local self-attention with global state space layers (Jamba, recurrent-attention hybrids), associative recall capacity, and empirical trade-offs.

modules.outcome: implement a discrete Linear State Space Model with parallel associative scan in PyTorch and contrast associative recall accuracy against vanilla multi-head attention.

modules.name: Capstone: Build and Train an Autoregressive Transformer with RoPE and FlashAttention

objectives.text: Build a complete modern decoder-only Transformer language model from scratch in PyTorch incorporating state-of-the-art architectural advancements.
Implement custom Multi-Head Attention featuring Grouped-Query Attention (GQA) and Rotary Position Embeddings (RoPE).
Integrate FlashAttention (or custom tiled attention) to enable memory-efficient training over extended sequence context windows.
Implement RMSNorm for pre-normalization and SwiGLU activation functions within the MLP blocks.
Implement Byte-Pair Encoding (BPE) tokenization or integrate Tiktoken / SentencePiece tokenizers with proper special token handling.
Implement causal autoregressive cross-entropy loss with label smoothing and gradient clipping.
Train the model on a real-world text corpus (e.g. TinyStories or OpenWebText subset) using the AdamW optimizer and cosine learning rate schedule with linear warmup.
Implement top-k, top-p (nucleus), temperature sampling, and key-value cache (KV cache) decoding for efficient autoregressive text generation.
Conduct ablation studies comparing: (1) Sinusoidal vs RoPE positional embeddings, (2) Pre-LN vs Post-LN stability, and (3) standard MHA vs GQA inference throughput and memory usage.

modules.finalResult: a verified, high-performance Transformer codebase with RoPE, GQA, and KV caching, complete with an ablation report analyzing generation quality and memory efficiency.

completionOutcomes: Formulate autoregressive sequence modeling in terms of conditional joint probability factorization.
Explain the mathematical necessity of the 1/sqrt(d_k) scaling factor in dot-product attention.
Derive the computational FLOPs and activation memory complexity of multi-head self-attention.
Implement causal lower-triangular masking for autoregressive language models.
Contrast Pre-LayerNorm and Post-LayerNorm in deep Transformer stability and signal propagation.
Derive Rotary Position Embeddings (RoPE) mathematically using complex representation.
Explain ALiBi and contrast its length extrapolation properties with absolute positional encodings.
Analyze the GPU memory hierarchy and explain why standard attention is memory-bandwidth bound.
Explain the online Softmax formulation that makes FlashAttention tiling mathematically exact.
Analyze the memory footprint of the Key-Value (KV) cache during autoregressive generation.
Derive continuous-time linear state space models and their discretized recurrent/convolutional forms.
Explain the selective state space mechanism of Mamba and its hardware-aware associative scan.
Implement Grouped-Query Attention (GQA) and calculate its memory bandwidth reduction factor.
Implement top-p (nucleus) and temperature sampling over output logits.
Build and train an end-to-end decoder-only Transformer from scratch on a text corpus.
Measure tokens-per-second and memory utilization during training and inference.

Progression: Recurrent & Attention Foundations → Scaled Dot-Product & Transformer Anatomy → Positional Encodings & RoPE → FlashAttention & Memory Hierarchy → State Space Models & Mamba → Transformer Training Capstone.

levels.title: Representation Learning & Latent Metric Spaces
levels.scope: examine how deep neural networks learn semantically rich representations without human labels: contrastive learning, self-supervised objectives, metric learning, the manifold hypothesis, and dense vector spaces.

modules.name: The Manifold Hypothesis & Self-Supervised Objectives

objectives.text: Understand the Manifold Hypothesis: real-world high-dimensional data (images, text, audio) concentrates on lower-dimensional non-linear sub-manifolds.
Study linear dimensionality reduction: Principal Component Analysis (PCA) derivation via maximum variance and minimum reconstruction error, probabilistic PCA.

Analyze non-linear dimensionality reduction: t-SNE (t-Distributed Stochastic Neighbor Embedding, perplexity, Student-t distribution) and UMAP (Uniform Manifold Approximation and Projection, Riemannian geometry basics).
Master self-supervised pretext tasks: autoencoding, masked language modeling (BERT), masked image modeling (MAE, He et al.), and autoregressive prediction as representation learners.
Analyze the reconstruction versus contrastive objective trade-off: pixel-level reconstruction wasting capacity on high-frequency details vs semantic feature extraction.

modules.outcome: derive PCA analytically using Rayleigh quotients and implement a Masked Autoencoder (MAE) baseline that reconstructs masked image patches.

modules.name: Contrastive Learning Theory & InfoNCE

objectives.text: Master Contrastive Representation Learning: pulling positive pairs together while pushing negative pairs apart in a metric embedding space.
Derive the InfoNCE loss function (Oord et al., CPC): connection to Noise-Contrastive Estimation (NCE) and mutual information maximization lower bound.
Analyze SimCLR (Chen et al.): composition of data augmentations, projection head non-linearity, temperature parameter tau, and large batch size dynamics.
Understand Representation Collapse: the trivial constant-representation failure mode in contrastive learning and mechanisms to prevent it.
Study Momentum Contrast (MoCo, He et al.): decoupling dictionary size from batch size using a dynamic memory queue and momentum-updated target encoder.
Investigate Non-Contrastive Self-Supervision: BYOL (Bootstrap Your Own Latent, Grill et al.) and SimSiam (Chen & He) avoiding collapse without negative pairs using stop-gradient operators.
Analyze Barlow Twins (Zbontar et al.) and VICReg (Bardes et al.): information-theoretic objectives enforcing invariance, variance preservation, and cross-correlation decorrelation.

modules.outcome: prove mathematically that InfoNCE loss optimizes a variational lower bound on mutual information between views, and implement SimCLR with InfoNCE loss in PyTorch.

modules.name: Metric Learning, Deep Embeddings & Triplet Geometries

objectives.text: Understand Metric Learning: learning distance metrics d(x_i, x_j) such that semantically similar items have small distances while dissimilar items have large distances.
Master Contrastive Loss (Hadsell et al.) and Triplet Loss (Schroff et al., FaceNet): anchor, positive, and negative geometries, and margin hyperparameter alpha.
Analyze Negative Mining Strategies: offline vs online negative mining, hard negative mining, semi-hard negative mining, and easy negative saturation.
Explore Angular and Cosine Margin Losses: SphereFace, CosFace, and ArcFace (Additive Angular Margin Loss, Deng et al.) for discriminative feature spaces.
Understand embedding normalization: why projecting representations onto the unit hypersphere S^(d-1) stabilizes cosine distance metrics and temperature scaling.
Study properties of representations on hyperspheres: Wang & Isola's alignment (closeness of positive pairs) and uniformity (uniform distribution over the hypersphere) metrics.

modules.outcome: implement ArcFace with angular margin in PyTorch and compute Wang & Isola alignment and uniformity scores for learned representations.

modules.name: Dense Vector Retrieval & Semantic Search Science

objectives.text: Formulate the information retrieval task in dense representation spaces: bi-encoder architectures, cross-encoder rerankers, and dual-encoder scaling.
Analyze dual-encoder training: in-batch negatives, hard negative mining (BM25 negatives vs dense retrieval negatives), and multi-stage distillation (ColBERT, late interaction).
Understand the geometry of high-dimensional vector spaces: orthogonality of random vectors, concentration of distances, and hubness problem.
Analyze Exact Nearest Neighbor (k-NN) search complexity and the theoretical limits of sub-linear retrieval in high dimensions.
Study Approximate Nearest Neighbor (ANN) algorithms: graph-based indexing (Hierarchical Navigable Small World, HNSW), inverted file indexes (IVF), and product quantization (PQ).
Evaluate dense retrieval quality using ranking metrics: Mean Reciprocal Rank (MRR@k), Normalized Discounted Cumulative Gain (NDCG@k), and Recall@k.

modules.outcome: implement a bi-encoder dense retriever with hard negative mining, index embeddings using HNSW, and measure NDCG@10 on a search benchmark.

modules.name: Probing & Analyzing Latent Representations

objectives.text: Understand Representation Probing: testing what linguistic or perceptual information is linearly decodable from intermediate neural activations (Alain & Ollivier).
Master Linear Probing: training frozen linear classifiers on intermediate representations and interpreting probe accuracy as information presence.
Analyze the limitations and caveats of linear probes: differentiating between information extraction versus computation, and probe complexity trade-offs (Hewitt & Liang control tasks).
Study Centered Kernel Alignment (CKA, Kornblith et al.): comparing representations across different architectures, layers, and random initializations invariantly to orthogonal rotations.
Analyze Intrinsic Dimension Estimation: Two-NN algorithm, maximum likelihood estimators, and tracking how intrinsic dimension changes across deep network layers.
Examine Anisotropy in Language Model Embeddings: representation degeneration, singular value decay, and embedding cluster geometry in hyperspherical spaces.

modules.outcome: implement Centered Kernel Alignment (CKA) from mathematical scratch and compare the layer-wise representational similarity between two trained models.

modules.name: Capstone: Self-Supervised Representation Reproduction and Latent Geometry Probing

objectives.text: Reproduce a seminal self-supervised representation learning method (SimCLR or Masked Autoencoder) on an unlabelled scientific image or text dataset.
Implement the full data augmentation pipeline, encoder network, non-linear projection head, and InfoNCE / reconstruction objective.
Track empirical alignment and uniformity metrics over the unit hypersphere throughout training to monitor representation geometry.
Evaluate learned representations using standard linear probing protocol: freeze the encoder backbone and train a linear classification probe on extracted representations.
Implement Centered Kernel Alignment (CKA) to visualize cross-layer representational similarity and observe where abstract representations emerge.
Conduct an ablation study comparing: (1) with vs without non-linear projection head, (2) temperature scaling variations in InfoNCE, and (3) hard negative mining vs random negatives.
Evaluate out-of-distribution transfer performance of the learned representations against a fully supervised baseline.
Write a scientific research report presenting t-SNE / UMAP latent visualizations, CKA heatmaps, alignment-uniformity scatter plots, and linear probe accuracy curves.

modules.finalResult: a reproducible self-supervised representation codebase and research paper evaluating latent space geometry and downstream transfer capabilities.

completionOutcomes: Explain the Manifold Hypothesis and formulate representation learning in terms of low-dimensional manifolds.
Derive the analytical formulation of Principal Component Analysis (PCA) using constrained optimization.
Explain the mathematical objective of t-SNE and its use of the Student-t distribution to resolve crowding.
Derive the InfoNCE loss function and prove its connection to mutual information maximization.
Explain the representation collapse problem in self-supervised learning and how BYOL and SimSiam avoid it.
Derive the Triplet Loss and compare hard negative mining and semi-hard negative mining strategies.
Implement ArcFace (Additive Angular Margin Loss) and explain why angular margins encourage intra-class compactness.
Quantify representation quality on the unit hypersphere using Wang & Isola's alignment and uniformity metrics.
Contrast bi-encoder and cross-encoder architectures in terms of accuracy, inference latency, and indexing feasibility.
Explain how Hierarchical Navigable Small World (HNSW) graphs achieve approximate logarithmic nearest neighbor search.
Compute standard ranking evaluation metrics including MRR@k and NDCG@k from scratch.
Train linear probes on frozen neural network representations and evaluate probe task performance.
Implement Centered Kernel Alignment (CKA) and construct cross-model representation similarity matrices.
Identify anisotropy in transformer representations and explain why word embeddings tend to collapse into narrow cones.

Progression: Manifold Hypothesis & Dimensionality Reduction → Contrastive Learning & InfoNCE → Metric Learning & Hyperspherical Geometries → Dense Vector Retrieval → Representation Probing & CKA → Self-Supervised Reproduction Capstone.

levels.title: Reinforcement Learning & Sequential Decision Theory
levels.scope: explore the mathematical foundations of sequential decision making under uncertainty: Markov Decision Processes, Bellman equations, dynamic programming, policy gradients, actor-critic algorithms, and model-based reinforcement learning.

modules.name: Markov Decision Processes & Bellman Optimality

objectives.text: Formulate the Reinforcement Learning problem as a Markov Decision Process (MDP): states S, actions A, transition probability function P(s'|s, a), reward function R(s, a), and discount factor gamma.
Define trajectories, discounted return G_t, policy pi(a|s), state-value function V^pi(s), and action-value function Q^pi(s, a).
Derive the Bellman Expectation Equations for V^pi(s) and Q^pi(s, a) using the law of total expectation.
Define optimal policy pi^*, optimal state-value V^*(s), and optimal action-value Q^*(s, a).
Derive the Bellman Optimality Equations: non-linear system of equations incorporating max operators over actions.
Prove the Bellman operator is a contraction mapping in the supremum norm via Banach Fixed-Point Theorem, ensuring convergence to a unique fixed point.
Implement Dynamic Programming algorithms for known MDPs: Policy Iteration (policy evaluation + policy improvement theorem) and Value Iteration.

modules.outcome: prove the contraction mapping property of the Bellman optimality operator and implement exact Value Iteration for discrete MDP environments.

modules.name: Model-Free Value-Based Methods & Q-Learning

objectives.text: Understand the model-free setting where transition dynamics P(s'|s, a) and reward functions R(s, a) are unknown.
Analyze Monte Carlo (MC) methods: first-visit vs every-visit MC, high variance, zero bias, and requiring complete episodes.
Master Temporal Difference (TD) learning: TD(0) update rule, TD error delta_t, bootstrapping, and bias-variance trade-offs against Monte Carlo.
Contrast on-policy learning (SARSA) and off-policy learning (Q-learning) and analyze their exploration-exploitation convergence guarantees.
Study function approximation in Q-learning: linear function approximation, feature divergence, and the "deadly triad" (bootstrapping, off-policy learning, function approximation).
Master Deep Q-Networks (DQN, Mnih et al.): using neural networks to approximate Q(s, a), experience replay buffers to break temporal correlation, and target networks to stabilize regression targets.
Analyze improvements to DQN: Double DQN (mitigating maximization bias), Prioritized Experience Replay (PER), and Dueling DQN (decoupling state-value and advantage functions).

modules.outcome: derive Double DQN mathematically to prove how decoupled action selection and evaluation eliminates overestimation bias, and train a DQN agent on a classic control environment.

modules.name: Policy Gradient Theorems & Actor-Critic Architectures

objectives.text: Understand parameterized policies pi_theta(a|s) and formulate the expected trajectory return objective J(theta).
Derive the Policy Gradient Theorem analytically using the log-derivative trick (likelihood ratio): grad_theta J(theta) = E[grad_theta log pi_theta(a|s) * Q(s, a)].
Analyze the REINFORCE algorithm (Williams): Monte Carlo policy gradient, empirical sample averages, and high variance limitations.
Introduce baselines to policy gradients: proving mathematically that state-dependent baselines b(s) reduce variance without introducing any bias to the gradient estimate.
Define the Advantage Function: A(s, a) = Q(s, a) - V(s), and formulate Advantage Actor-Critic (A2C/A3C) architectures.
Analyze Generalized Advantage Estimation (GAE, Schulman et al.): compounding n-step TD errors via exponential decay parameter lambda to tune bias-variance trade-offs.
Understand policy parameterization for continuous action spaces: Gaussian policies with learnable mean and state-independent or state-dependent log variance.

modules.outcome: derive the Policy Gradient Theorem on paper and implement Generalized Advantage Estimation (GAE) with analytical variance analysis.

modules.name: Advanced Policy Optimization: TRPO, PPO & Soft Actor-Critic

objectives.text: Analyze the step-size problem in policy gradient methods: large parameter updates causing catastrophic policy collapse in non-stationary RL landscapes.
Study Trust Region Policy Optimization (TRPO, Schulman et al.): surrogate objective, monotonic improvement guarantee, and enforcing a hard KL divergence constraint D_KL(pi_old || pi_new) <= delta.
Understand natural policy gradients and Fisher Information Matrix approximations using conjugate gradient methods to compute trust-region steps.
Master Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO, Schulman et al.): PPO-Clip surrogate objective with clipped probability ratios r_t(theta) to constrain updates without second-order Hessians.
Analyze the entropy bonus in policy objectives to encourage exploration and prevent premature policy convergence to deterministic sub-optimal actions.
Master Maximum Entropy Reinforcement Learning: Soft Actor-Critic (SAC, Haarnoja et al.), entropy-augmented reward, soft Bellman equation, and continuous off-policy stability.
Compare on-policy (PPO) versus off-policy (SAC) sample efficiency, wall-clock compute requirements, and optimization stability.

modules.outcome: derive the PPO clipped surrogate objective and implement a complete PPO actor-critic training pipeline in PyTorch.

modules.name: Model-Based Reinforcement Learning & Search

objectives.text: Understand Model-Based Reinforcement Learning (MBRL): learning transition dynamics models f_theta(s, a) = s' and planning via simulated rollouts.
Analyze model bias and compounding error: why small inaccuracies in learned environment dynamics amplify exponentially over multi-step planning horizons.
Master Model Predictive Control (MPC): shooting methods, cross-entropy method (CEM), and online replanning at every environmental time step.
Study Dyna-Q architecture: interleaving real-world experience, model learning, and simulated experience replay for sample-efficient policy improvement.
Analyze Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS): selection (PUCT algorithm), expansion, simulation / rollout, and backpropagation phases.
Study AlphaZero and MuZero principles (Silver et al., Schrittwieser et al.): unifying deep neural networks with MCTS planning without explicit environment rules.

modules.outcome: implement a learned transition model with Model Predictive Control (MPC) and evaluate compounding prediction error over varying rollout depths.

modules.name: Capstone: Benchmark PPO vs Soft Actor-Critic on Continuous Control with Ablation Analysis

objectives.text: Design an empirical research benchmark comparing on-policy Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) against off-policy Soft Actor-Critic (SAC) on continuous control environments (e.g. Gymnasium HalfCheetah / Ant / InvertedPendulum).
Implement PPO with Generalized Advantage Estimation (GAE), orthogonal weight initialization, gradient clipping, and value function clipping.
Implement Soft Actor-Critic (SAC) with twin Q-networks (clipped double-Q trick), target smoothing (Polyak averaging tau), and automatic entropy temperature tuning (alpha).
Conduct controlled experiments across at least 5 distinct random seeds to compute statistically sound learning curves with 95% confidence intervals.
Perform systematic ablation studies on PPO: (1) effect of clipping epsilon (0.1, 0.2, 0.3), (2) GAE lambda trade-off between bias and variance, and (3) presence vs absence of value function clipping.
Perform systematic ablation studies on SAC: (1) fixed entropy temperature vs automatic entropy adjustment, and (2) target update rate tau.
Compare sample efficiency (environment steps to reach reward threshold) and wall-clock training time between PPO and SAC.
Draft a comprehensive academic research paper summarizing findings, plotting reward trajectories with variance bands, and analyzing stability failure modes.

modules.finalResult: a reproducible deep RL benchmark codebase and research paper evaluating on-policy vs off-policy policy optimization algorithms.

completionOutcomes: Formulate continuous and discrete decision problems as Markov Decision Processes.
Derive the Bellman Expectation and Optimality equations from first principles.
Prove that the Bellman optimality operator is a gamma-contraction mapping using the Banach Fixed-Point Theorem.
Implement Policy Iteration and Value Iteration for discrete state-action spaces.
Explain the deadly triad in reinforcement learning: bootstrapping, function approximation, and off-policy learning.
Implement Deep Q-Networks (DQN) with experience replay and target networks.
Derive Double DQN and explain how it resolves the maximization bias of standard Q-learning.
Derive the Policy Gradient Theorem using the likelihood ratio trick.
Prove that subtracting a state-dependent baseline from policy gradients introduces zero bias while reducing variance.
Implement Generalized Advantage Estimation (GAE) and explain the role of the lambda parameter.
Explain the mathematical motivation for Trust Region Policy Optimization (TRPO) and the KL constraint.
Derive the clipped surrogate objective of Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO).
Formulate the Maximum Entropy RL framework and explain how Soft Actor-Critic (SAC) balances exploration and exploitation.
Explain compounding prediction error in model-based RL and how Model Predictive Control mitigates drift.
Implement the four phases of Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) with PUCT action selection.
Conduct reproducible RL experiments with multiple random seeds, reporting mean returns and confidence intervals.
Progression: MDPs & Bellman Contractions → Model-Free Q-Learning & DQN → Policy Gradients & Advantage Actor-Critic → PPO & Soft Actor-Critic → Model-Based RL & MCTS → Deep RL Benchmark Capstone.

levels.title: Reasoning, Planning & Test-Time Compute
levels.scope: investigate the frontiers of machine reasoning in language and multimodal systems: chain-of-thought mechanics, search over thought spaces, outcome versus process reward models, test-time compute scaling laws, and self-correction dynamics.

modules.name: Foundations of Machine Reasoning & Chain-of-Thought

objectives.text: Define reasoning in computational systems: deductive, inductive, abductive reasoning, and multi-step symbolic manipulation.
Analyze Chain-of-Thought (CoT, Wei et al.): prompting models to produce intermediate computational tokens before emitting final answers.
Theoretical analysis of CoT expressivity: why allowing models intermediate tokens increases the computational class of constant-depth Transformers (Merrill & Sabharwal).
Examine reasoning capacity versus model scale: emergent reasoning abilities, phase changes, and non-linear accuracy jumps on complex benchmarks.
Study Least-to-Most Prompting and Problem Decomposition: recursive reduction of hard reasoning problems into simpler sub-goals.
Analyze Failure Modes of CoT: unfaithful reasoning (reasoning traces not matching actual underlying model computation), post-hoc rationalization, and error accumulation.

modules.outcome: derive theoretical circuit complexity proofs demonstrating why chain-of-thought expands the computational capability of fixed-depth transformers.

modules.name: Search Over Thought Spaces & Tree Search Algorithms

objectives.text: Move beyond linear left-to-right generation: conceptualizing problem-solving as search over combinatorial thought spaces.
Analyze Tree of Thoughts (ToT, Yao et al.): state evaluation, thought generation, and systematic tree exploration via Breadth-First Search (BFS) and Depth-First Search (DFS).
Study Graph of Thoughts (GoT, Besta et al.): modeling reasoning as arbitrary directed acyclic graphs allowing thought combination, branching, and feedback loops.
Integrate Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) with language models: thought state evaluation, exploration-exploitation trade-offs (PUCT), and lookahead simulations.
Analyze Search Heuristics: self-evaluation prompts, perplexity scoring, and external symbolic verifiers (Python interpreters, SMT solvers, Lean/Isabelle theorem provers).
Study A* and Best-First Search on reasoning trees: designing admissible heuristic cost functions for language model search navigation.

modules.outcome: implement a Tree of Thoughts search engine with backtracking and heuristic thought evaluation on complex algorithmic or mathematical puzzles.

modules.name: Verifiers, Reward Models & Process Supervision

objectives.text: Analyze the fundamental verification versus generation asymmetry: why verifying a proposed solution is often computationally easier than generating it (NP-completeness analogy).
Master Outcome-based Reward Models (ORMs, Cobbe et al.): scoring complete reasoning trajectories based solely on final answer correctness.
Analyze the credit assignment failure in ORMs: penalizing valid intermediate reasoning when a final minor arithmetic mistake occurs, and rewarding false reasoning that stumbles upon correct answers.
Master Process-Supervised Reward Models (PRMs, Lightman et al., Let's Verify Step by Step): scoring every single intermediate reasoning step individually.
Compare PRM versus ORM data collection: human step-level annotation costs vs automated synthetic step-level labeling (e.g. Monte Carlo rollouts from intermediate states).
Formulate Best-of-N (Rejection Sampling) decoding with PRMs: generating N independent reasoning paths and selecting the trajectory that maximizes the cumulative or minimum PRM step score.
Study Majority Voting (Self-Consistency, Wang et al.): sampling multiple temperature-varied reasoning paths and taking the modal final answer.

modules.outcome: train a Process Reward Model on step-annotated mathematical reasoning data and compare Best-of-N selection accuracy against an Outcome Reward Model.

modules.name: Test-Time Compute & Inference Scaling Laws

objectives.text: Formulate the Test-Time Compute frontier: trading off training compute, pre-training parameter scale, and test-time evaluation compute.
Analyze Inference-Time Scaling Laws (Snell et al., Brown et al.): empirical relationships between floating point operations expended at inference and final task accuracy.

Study strategies for allocating test-time compute: (1) sampling-based search (Best-of-N, Beam Search), (2) iterative refinement and revision loops, and (3) adaptive compute allocation based on problem difficulty.
Examine Test-Time Compute vs Pre-Training Compute efficiency: determining when expending 10x more test-time tokens outperforms scaling model parameters by 10x.
Analyze System 1 (fast, intuitive autoregressive generation) versus System 2 (slow, deliberative search and verification) cognitive architectures in foundation models.

Examine reasoning models trained with large-scale reinforcement learning over search chains (e.g. DeepSeek-R1, OpenAI o1 style): self-generated reflection tokens, backtrack tokens, and long-horizon exploration.

modules.outcome: formulate mathematical scaling curves measuring accuracy improvements as a function of test-time sample budgets and fit Pareto frontiers.

modules.name: Self-Correction, Reflection & Reasoning Distillation

objectives.text: Analyze Intrinsic Self-Correction: can language models accurately identify and correct their own reasoning errors without external ground-truth feedback? (Huang et al., Kamoi et al.).
Study the limitations of unassisted self-correction: model sycophancy, degradation of initially correct answers under self-critique, and over-confidence in hallucinations.
Examine External-Feedback Self-Correction: incorporating compiler errors, unit test executions, and verifiable formal logic checks into iterative reflection loops (Reflexion, Shinn et al.).
Study Reasoning Distillation: fine-tuning smaller student models on synthetic CoT and MCTS search traces generated by large frontier reasoning models.
Analyze the risk of superficial pattern imitation during distillation: student models mimicking the linguistic style of reasoning without internalizing the underlying search and verification logic.

modules.outcome: implement an automated reflection loop paired with a Python code execution verifier and measure the empirical rate of successful error correction versus degradation.

modules.name: Capstone: Train a Process Reward Model and Build a Tree-Search Reasoning Engine

objectives.text: Design an end-to-end research experiment developing a verified reasoning engine for challenging mathematical or competitive programming problems (e.g. GSM8K / MATH / Olympiad problems).
Construct a step-by-step reasoning dataset containing both valid steps and synthetically introduced reasoning errors (divergence points).
Train a Process Reward Model (PRM) by fine-tuning an open-weight foundation model to predict binary validity labels for each intermediate step delimiter.
Implement Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) decoding and Best-of-N rejection sampling guided by the trained PRM step scores.

Conduct an empirical study measuring accuracy against inference compute budgets across: (1) Greedy decoding, (2) Self-Consistency with majority voting (N=1 to N=64), (3) Best-of-N with ORM, and (4) MCTS guided by PRM.
Plot test-time compute scaling curves: accuracy vs total generation tokens and FLOPs expended per problem.
Perform qualitative error analysis categorizing remaining failure modes: deceptive reasoning traces that fool the PRM, early tree search pruning errors, and calculation mistakes.
Draft an academic research paper documenting the methodology, PRM training dynamics, empirical scaling laws, and reproducibility artifacts.

modules.finalResult: a verified PRM model checkpoint, MCTS reasoning search engine codebase, and academic paper analyzing test-time compute scaling dynamics.

completionOutcomes: Explain how chain-of-thought increases the computational expressive power of constant-depth transformers.
Analyze the difference between faithful reasoning traces and post-hoc rationalizations in LLMs.
Implement the Tree of Thoughts (ToT) search algorithm with state evaluation and backtracking.
Formulate Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) over intermediate reasoning token sequences.
Explain why solution verification exhibits favorable computational complexity compared to solution generation.
Derive the credit assignment problem in Outcome-based Reward Models (ORMs).
Train a Process-Supervised Reward Model (PRM) to score individual intermediate reasoning steps.
Implement Best-of-N rejection sampling and evaluate the accuracy boost over greedy decoding.
Explain the mathematical mechanics of Self-Consistency and modal answer aggregation.
Formulate and fit empirical scaling laws relating test-time compute budget to reasoning accuracy.
Contrast System 1 intuitive autoregressive generation with System 2 deliberative search architectures.
Analyze the empirical limits of intrinsic self-correction without external environmental feedback.
Implement iterative reflection loops coupled with external symbolic verifiers and interpreters.
Distill high-compute reasoning traces into smaller, low-latency student models safely.
Conduct rigorous experiments evaluating reasoning capability across verified benchmark suites.

Progression: Chain-of-Thought Foundations → Search Over Thought Trees & MCTS → Outcome vs Process Reward Models → Test-Time Compute Scaling Laws → Self-Correction & Distillation → PRM & Tree Search Capstone.

levels.title: Research Evaluation Methodology & Benchmarking Science
levels.scope: master scientific rigor in artificial intelligence evaluation: statistical hypothesis testing, confidence intervals, benchmark contamination detection, Elo rating systems, automated evaluation theory, and reproducibility protocols.

modules.name: Statistical Hypothesis Testing & Significance in ML

objectives.text: Understand why raw metric differences (e.g. 0.8% accuracy improvement) are scientifically meaningless without statistical significance testing.
Formulate Null Hypothesis Significance Testing (NHST): null hypothesis H_0, alternative hypothesis H_1, Type I error rate alpha, and Type II error rate beta (statistical power).
Analyze parametric tests (paired Student's t-test) and explain why their normality assumptions are frequently violated in machine learning benchmarks.
Master non-parametric tests: Wilcoxon signed-rank test for paired model comparisons and Mann-Whitney U test for independent samples.
Master Bootstrapping: non-parametric bootstrap resampling, constructing empirical bootstrap distributions, and computing 95% studentized bootstrap confidence intervals.
Understand Permutation Tests: exact non-parametric tests through random label permutation under the null hypothesis.
Address the Multiple Hypothesis Testing problem: family-wise error rate (FWER) inflation, Bonferroni correction, and Benjamini-Hochberg False Discovery Rate (FDR) control.

modules.outcome: implement non-parametric bootstrap confidence interval estimation and perform Benjamini-Hochberg corrections across multi-model benchmark results.

modules.name: Benchmark Design, Goodhart's Law & Dataset Contamination

objectives.text: Examine Goodhart's Law and Campbell's Law in AI evaluation: "When a measure becomes a target, it ceases to be a good measure."
Study Benchmark Saturation: how rapid community overfitting and hill-climbing render benchmarks (GLUE, SuperGLUE, SQuAD) obsolete.
Analyze Benchmark Contamination: test set leakage into web-scraped pre-training corpora via verbatim overlap, paraphrased overlap, or token translation.
Master Contamination Detection Techniques: n-gram decontamination (13-gram overlap filtering, Brown et al.), min-hash LSH deduplication, and perplexity anomaly analysis.
Study Memorization vs Generalization Probing: Carlini et al. prefix-probing techniques to detect whether a model has memorized specific benchmark questions.
Design Contamination-Robust Benchmarks: dynamic test sets, private holdouts, programmatic question generators, and continuous evaluation suites (e.g. Chatbot Arena, SWE-bench).
Analyze Evaluation Suite Methodologies: holistic evaluation frameworks like HELM (Holistic Evaluation of Language Models) balancing accuracy, calibration, robustness, bias, and efficiency.

modules.outcome: implement an n-gram decontamination pipeline that scans a pre-training corpus for exact and fuzzy benchmark overlaps, reporting contamination percentage.

modules.name: Elo Rating Systems & Pairwise Comparative Evaluation

objectives.text: Understand pairwise comparison evaluation: why ranking outputs comparatively is significantly more reliable and discriminative than absolute Likert scale scoring.
Derive the Elo Rating System: logistic win probability formula P(A wins) = 1 / (1 + 10^((R_B - R_A)/400)), rating update rules, and K-factor dynamics.
Study the Bradley-Terry-Luce (BTL) Model for paired comparisons: maximum likelihood estimation of underlying latent quality parameters from observed pairwise victories.
Analyze Bradley-Terry MLE estimation via logistic regression and iteratively reweighted least squares (IRLS).
Master Crowdsourced Evaluation Platforms: LMSYS Chatbot Arena methodology, handling tie games, length bias, conversational turn length, and user demographic bias.
Analyze Win-Rate Metrics: head-to-head win matrices, style-controlled win rates (adjusting for response length, markdown formatting, and tone), and bootstrap confidence intervals over Elo ranks.

modules.outcome: implement the Bradley-Terry model in Python and estimate latent model Elo ratings with 95% bootstrap confidence intervals from pairwise match records.

modules.name: Automated Evaluation Theory & Judge Model Biases

objectives.text: Analyze LLM-as-a-Judge: using large foundation models to automate evaluation of complex, open-ended, and non-deterministic model outputs (Zheng et al., MT-Bench).
Categorize and quantify systematic biases in judge models:
Position bias: the tendency of LLM judges to favor the first presented candidate response (Option A vs Option B).
Mitigating position bias: swapping candidate order and requiring consistency, or averaging bidirectional scores.
Length bias: the systematic tendency of judge models to score longer, more verbose answers higher regardless of factual density or accuracy.
Self-enhancement bias: foundation models rating responses generated by their own family or architecture systematically higher than competitor models.
Authority and formatting biases: models over-indexing on markdown styling, polite conversational disclaimers, and authoritative tone over logical correctness.
Measure inter-annotator agreement: Cohen's Kappa, Fleiss' Kappa, and Krippendorff's Alpha between human experts and LLM judges.
Calibration and error bars: calculating judge model calibration curves and Expected Calibration Error (ECE) for classification and grading tasks.

modules.outcome: construct a swap-paired evaluation protocol that measures and cancels out positional bias and quantifies length bias in automated judges.

modules.name: Reproducibility Protocols, Artifact Packaging & Open Science

objectives.text: Understand the AI Reproducibility Crisis: missing random seeds, undocumented hardware environments, unpinned library versions, and non-deterministic CUDA operations.
Analyze sources of non-determinism in deep learning: CUDA atomic operations, cuDNN benchmark algorithms, multi-threaded data loaders, and floating point non-associativity.
Establish gold-standard reproducibility protocols: deterministic seed setting (Python, NumPy, PyTorch, CUDA), environment containerization (Docker, Nix), and code release standards.
Master Artifact Packaging for Conferences (NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR): open-source code repositories, model weight checkpoints, training logs, evaluation scripts, and reproducible notebooks.
Understand Scientific Reporting Standards: clear reporting of total compute budget (GPU hours, hardware specifications, estimated carbon footprint), negative results, and failure modes.

modules.outcome: package a machine learning project into a fully reproducible, one-click artifact verifying identical evaluation scores across different machines.

modules.name: Capstone: Build a Contamination-Robust Reasoning Benchmark with Statistical Significance Testing

objectives.text: Design and build a scientifically rigorous evaluation benchmark suite for assessing mathematical and scientific reasoning.
Construct a dataset of novel, human-curated or programmatically generated reasoning problems with verifiable ground-truth solutions.
Implement an automated contamination detection scan that verifies zero leakage against public training corpora using 13-gram overlap and embedding cosine similarity checks.
Evaluate at least four distinct open-weight foundation models across zero-shot and chain-of-thought prompting configurations.
Perform pairwise comparison evaluation across all model outputs using both human evaluation and a debiased, position-swapped LLM-as-a-Judge.
Fit a Bradley-Terry model to the pairwise matchup outcomes and calculate Elo ratings with 95% bootstrap confidence intervals.
Conduct rigorous non-parametric hypothesis testing (Wilcoxon signed-rank test with Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction) to establish whether observed performance gaps are statistically significant.
Produce a comprehensive academic evaluation report (NeurIPS benchmark track formatting) complete with reliability metrics (Fleiss' Kappa), length bias ablation, and contamination certificates.

modules.finalResult: an open-source, contamination-free evaluation benchmark with statistical significance verification and automated debiased judge tooling.

completionOutcomes: Formulate null hypothesis significance testing for machine learning model comparisons.
Implement non-parametric bootstrap resampling to calculate rigorous 95% confidence intervals.
Apply Benjamini-Hochberg False Discovery Rate corrections across multiple hypothesis test runs.
Explain Goodhart's law in the context of AI benchmarks and public leaderboards.
Implement n-gram overlap algorithms to detect benchmark contamination in pre-training data.
Probe model memorization using prefix-matching and perplexity anomaly analysis.
Derive the Bradley-Terry-Luce model and calculate maximum likelihood Elo ratings.
Analyze systematic biases in LLM judges including position bias, length bias, and self-enhancement bias.
Implement position-swapping protocols to eliminate positional preference in automated evaluations.
Calculate Cohen's Kappa, Fleiss' Kappa, and Krippendorff's Alpha to measure inter-annotator agreement.
Quantify Expected Calibration Error (ECE) for probabilistic classification and judging models.
Identify and mitigate sources of non-determinism in PyTorch and CUDA operations.
Create gold-standard reproducible scientific artifacts conforming to NeurIPS / ICML standards.
Critique published AI research papers for statistical flaws, cherry-picked baselines, or contaminated test sets.

Progression: Statistical Significance & Bootstrapping → Benchmark Contamination & Memorization → Pairwise Comparison & Elo Ratings → Automated Judge Biases → Reproducibility Standards → Contamination-Robust Benchmark Capstone.

levels.title: Alignment Theory, Robustness & Interpretability
levels.scope: investigate the mathematical foundations of AI alignment, adversarial robustness, and mechanistic interpretability: preference optimization theory, reward hacking, linear representation hypothesis, circuits, induction heads, and activation steering.

modules.name: Preference Learning Theory: RLHF, DPO & Beyond

objectives.text: Formulate the Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) objective: maximizing expected reward while penalizing divergence from reference policy via KL divergence D_KL(pi_theta || pi_ref).
Analyze Reward Model Training: Bradley-Terry pairwise preference loss log sigma(r(x, y_w) - r(x, y_l)) and margin calibration.

Analyze Reward Hacking and Overoptimization: Goodhart's law in RLHF, where the policy exploits flaws in the learned reward model to achieve high reward without satisfying true human intent (Gao et al.).

Derive Direct Preference Optimization (DPO, Rafailov et al.) mathematically: expressing the optimal policy analytically in terms of ground-truth reward and substituting into the Bradley-Terry objective.
Prove that DPO implicitly optimizes the exact same objective as PPO-based RLHF without training a separate reward model or executing reinforcement learning loops.
Analyze generalizations and variants of DPO: Identity Preference Optimization (IPO, Azar et al.), Kahneman-Tversky Optimization (KTO, Ethayarajh et al.), and Simple Preference Optimization (SimPO).
Investigate Online and Iterative DPO: on-policy negative sampling, self-play preference tuning, and preventing off-policy distribution shift.

modules.outcome: derive the closed-form relationship between reward functions and optimal policies in DPO, and implement DPO loss from scratch in PyTorch.

modules.name: Adversarial Robustness, Jailbreaks & Safety Bounds

objectives.text: Formulate adversarial attacks as constrained optimization problems: finding minimal perturbation delta under L_p norm bound that changes model output.
Analyze classical adversarial attacks on vision models: Fast Gradient Sign Method (FGSM, Goodfellow et al.), Projected Gradient Descent (PGD, Madry et al.), and Carlini-Wagner (CW) attacks.
Study Adversarial Training: minimax optimization min_theta E[max_{||delta||<=epsilon} L(theta, x + delta, y)] and its robustness guarantees.
Analyze Adversarial Vulnerabilities in Language Models: token-level gradient attacks (Greedy Coordinate Gradient, GCG, Zou et al.), suffix optimization, and universal transferable jailbreaks.
Examine Multimodal Jailbreaks: exploiting vision encoders with imperceptible adversarial perturbations that bypass text-based safety guardrails.
Analyze the Safety Alignment Tax: trade-offs where aggressive refusal training reduces model helpfulness, reasoning ability, or mathematical competence.
