modules.outcome: implement Projected Gradient Descent (PGD) adversarial attack on neural representations and evaluate model accuracy drops under bounded perturbations.

modules.name: Mechanistic Interpretability: Circuits & Induction Heads

objectives.text: Understand the goal of Mechanistic Interpretability: reverse-engineering deep neural network weights and activations into human-understandable computational algorithms and circuits (Olah et al.).
Study the Linear Representation Hypothesis: high-level semantic concepts are represented as linear directions (one-dimensional subspaces) in activation space (Elhage et al.).
Analyze the Transformer as a Residual Stream: viewing layers as reading from and writing to a shared communication bus rather than transforming representations sequentially.
Decompose Self-Attention Mathematically: QK-circuit (determining where information moves) and OV-circuit (determining what information is written to the residual stream).

Master Induction Heads (Olsson et al.): two-layer attention circuit that detects and continues repeated token sequences [A][B] ... [A] -> [B], forming the fundamental mechanism of in-context learning.
Study Polysemanticity and Superposition (Anthropic): models representing more features than they have dimensions by packing non-orthogonal vectors into high-dimensional space.
Analyze Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs): training L1-regularized overcomplete autoencoders on MLP activations to disentangle superposed representations into monosemantic features.

modules.outcome: implement an attention circuit visualization script that identifies induction heads in a small transformer model through copy-score metrics.

modules.name: Representation Engineering & Activation Steering

objectives.text: Understand Representation Engineering (RepE, Zou et al.): directly inspecting and manipulating the latent cognitive state of models rather than relying purely on prompt instructions.
Analyze Linear Artificial Tomography (LAT): extracting contrastive activation vectors for concepts like truthfulness, toxicity, sycophancy, or utility.
Master Activation Addition / Steering Vectors: adding a scaled concept direction vector (e.g. + alpha * v_truthful) to residual stream activations during inference.
Compare Steering Vectors versus Prompting: stability across long conversations, resistance to adversarial jailbreaking, and low computational overhead.
Examine Concept Erasing: null-space projections (Iterative Nullspace Projection, INLP, Ravfogel et al.) that completely remove sensitive concept directions from representations.
Analyze the trade-offs of representation steering: unintended collateral damage to language fluency, perplexity degradation, and concept leakage across related topics.

modules.outcome: extract a truthfulness steering vector by contrastive activation subtraction and demonstrate steerable suppression or elevation of honesty during text generation.

modules.name: Formal Verification & Auditing for Frontier AI Safety

objectives.text: Analyze Formal Verification of Neural Networks: proving mathematical guarantees that an input within a bounded region epsilon will never produce an unsafe output.
Study Interval Bound Propagation (IBP) and Crown: computing upper and lower bounds on layer activations to certify robustness.
Understand Scalability Limits of Formal Verification: why exact verification is NP-complete and remains intractable for billion-parameter foundation models.
Examine Red Teaming Methodologies: automated red-teaming agents, reinforcement learning for diverse vulnerability discovery (Perez et al.), and human expert evaluation loops.
Study Dangerous Capability Evaluations: autonomous replication benchmarks, cyberattack exploitation capabilities, chemical/biological weapon knowledge elicitation, and power-seeking behavior metrics.

modules.outcome: implement Interval Bound Propagation (IBP) for a multi-layer network and compute certified robustness bounds against bounded input perturbations.

modules.name: Capstone: Mechanistic Probing of Latent Truthfulness and Steering Vector Intervention

objectives.text: Design an empirical research project in mechanistic interpretability and alignment: investigating whether an open-weight foundation model internally represents truthfulness when it outputs false statements.
Curate a contrastive dataset of paired statements (True vs False across common misconceptions, factual trivia, and sycophantic traps).
Extract intermediate residual stream activations across all layers and token positions during forward passes.
Train linear probes (Logistic Regression / Ridge) on intermediate activations to classify truthfulness; identify the layers with maximum probe accuracy.
Extract a global Truthfulness Steering Vector using Contrastive Activation Addition (CAA): v = Mean(A_true) - Mean(A_false).
Inject the extracted steering vector into the residual stream at target layers during generation on hallucination-prone questions.
Measure the quantitative impact of activation steering across: (1) truthfulness accuracy, (2) refusal rate, and (3) generation perplexity and coherence.
Visualize attention head contributions and perform attribution patching to locate which specific attention heads write to the truthfulness subspace.
Draft a rigorous academic research paper detailing the linear representation hypothesis findings, ablation of steering magnitudes alpha, and limitations of activation editing.

modules.finalResult: an open-source mechanistic interpretability notebook and paper demonstrating extraction of truthfulness representations and activation steering intervention.

completionOutcomes: Formulate the RLHF objective and explain the role of the KL penalty against the reference policy.
Explain reward hacking and why overoptimizing a proxy reward degrades true model alignment.
Derive the Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) loss function mathematically from the Bradley-Terry model.
Explain the differences between DPO, IPO, and KTO in handling implicit reward constraints.
Implement Projected Gradient Descent (PGD) and explain adversarial perturbation bounds in L_p norm spaces.
Explain the mechanics of token-level gradient jailbreak attacks (such as GCG) on language models.
State the Linear Representation Hypothesis and describe how concepts are represented in activation space.
Decompose a Transformer layer into its QK-circuit and OV-circuit components.
Explain the function and mechanism of induction heads in in-context learning.
Explain the phenomenon of superposition and why models pack polysemantic features into activations.
Train a Sparse Autoencoder (SAE) to extract monosemantic dictionary features from residual stream activations.
Extract concept steering vectors using contrastive activation analysis.
Perform inference-time activation steering to modulate model behavior without fine-tuning weights.
Apply Interval Bound Propagation (IBP) to certify neural network robustness bounds.
Conduct red teaming audits to identify safety vulnerabilities and capability limits in foundation models.

Progression: Preference Learning Theory & DPO → Adversarial Robustness & Jailbreaks → Mechanistic Interpretability & Circuits → Activation Steering & Representation Engineering → Formal Safety Bounds → Truthfulness Probing Capstone.

levels.title: Foundation Model Pre-Training & Scaling Laws
levels.scope: explore the empirical science of large-scale foundation model pre-training: Kaplan versus Chinchilla scaling laws, compute-optimal allocation, synthetic data curation, pre-training loss dynamics, and tokenization frontiers.

modules.name: Empirical Scaling Laws: Kaplan vs Chinchilla

objectives.text: Understand the concept of empirical scaling laws in deep learning: power-law relationships L = (N_c / N)^alpha_N between loss, compute, data, and parameters.
Analyze Kaplan et al. (OpenAI 2020) scaling laws: power laws for cross-entropy loss as a function of model parameter count N, dataset size D, and training compute budget C.
Examine Kaplan's conclusion favoring scaling parameters over data: allocating compute primarily to model size while training on relatively small datasets.
Master Chinchilla Scaling Laws (Hoffmann et al., DeepMind 2022): identifying the suboptimal learning rate schedule and under-training flaw in Kaplan's methodology.
Analyze Hoffmann's three parametric fitting approaches: minimum loss envelopes, varying parameter count curves, and parametric loss modeling.
Derive the Chinchilla compute-optimal scaling rule: model parameters N and training tokens D should scale in equal proportion: N proportional to C^0.5, D proportional to C^0.5.
Understand Inference-Optimal vs Compute-Optimal Training: why frontier open-source models (Llama series) train on 15T+ tokens (far beyond Chinchilla optimal) to amortize inference serving costs.

modules.outcome: fit Chinchilla power-law parameters using non-linear least squares optimization over empirical loss checkpoints and compute optimal N and D for a target FLOP budget.

modules.name: Pre-Training Data Curation, Deduplication & Quality Filtering

objectives.text: Analyze the composition of frontier pre-training datasets (Common Crawl, RefinedWeb, FineWeb, RedPajama, The Stack): web text, books, papers, code, and conversations.
Study the impact of data quality on downstream performance: why filtering out low-quality web text improves model capability more than scaling model size by 2x.
Master Quality Filtering Algorithms: fastText heuristic classifiers trained on curated high-quality text (Wikipedia, textbooks) versus raw web scrapes.
Analyze Line-Level and Document-Level Heuristics: filtering based on word length distribution, punctuation ratios, repetition patterns, stop-word frequency, and perplexity filtering.
Master Text Deduplication: MinHash Locality-Sensitive Hashing (LSH), Jaccard similarity thresholds, and suffix array exact substring deduplication (Lee et al.).
Analyze the mathematical consequences of duplicate data: memorization risks, double-counting gradient updates, and loss of model generalization.
Examine Domain Mixing and Data Curricula: balancing web text, code, mathematics, and multilingual data, and scheduling high-quality tokens toward the end of training.

modules.outcome: implement a MinHash LSH deduplication pipeline and train a fastText quality filtering model to process and score raw web text.

modules.name: Synthetic Data Generation & Quality Filtering Science

objectives.text: Understand the impending web data exhaustion wall (Villalobos et al.) and the strategic role of synthetic data in foundation model training.
Analyze Synthetic Data Methodologies: self-instruct, evol-instruct (WizardLM), textbook generation (Textbooks Are All You Need, Phi series), and synthetic reasoning chains.

Study Synthetic Data Failure Modes: model collapse (Shumailov et al.), where training models iteratively on recursive generations leads to loss of rare tail knowledge and degenerative entropy collapse.
Examine Quality Filtering for Synthetic Data: using execution-based verifiers (unit tests for code, formal solvers for math), model judges, and diversity clustering.
Analyze Instruction-Backtranslation: using models to generate prompts for high-quality unlabelled web documents to produce synthetic instruction-response pairs at scale.

modules.outcome: design a synthetic question-answer generation pipeline with execution verification that avoids synthetic repetition collapse.

modules.name: Tokenization Frontiers & Vocabulary Science

objectives.text: Understand why tokenization is a critical inductive bias affecting arithmetic, code, multilingual performance, and safety.
Analyze Byte-Pair Encoding (BPE, Sennrich et al.): greedy frequency-based subword vocabulary construction and merge rules.
Analyze WordPiece (Schuster & Nakajima) and Unigram Language Model (Kudo, SentencePiece): probabilistic vocabulary pruning via language model likelihood reduction.
Examine Byte-Level Tokenization (BBPE): fallback to raw bytes to eliminate out-of-vocabulary (OOV) tokens completely.

Study Tokenization Failure Modes: digit tokenization causing arithmetic inability (tokenizing "1234" as single tokens vs individual digits), whitespace sensitivity, and prompt injection attacks in token space.
Explore Token-Free Architectures: character-level and byte-level foundation models (Megabyte, ByT5) and their trade-offs in context length and computational FLOPs.

modules.outcome: train a custom BPE tokenizer from raw text, inspect its merge table, and compare compression ratios across English, non-Latin scripts, and code.

modules.name: Pre-Training Dynamics, Loss Spikes & Numerical Stability

objectives.text: Analyze the loss curve trajectory during large-scale pre-training: power-law descent, plateauing, and learning rate decay phases.
Study Loss Spikes in Large-Scale Training: sudden divergence in loss accompanied by gradient norm explosion, and methods for mitigation.
Analyze the root causes of loss spikes: batch composition anomalies, attention logit growth, outlier features in hidden states, and FP16 underflow/overflow.
Master Numerical Stability Guards: QK-Norm (applying LayerNorm to queries and keys before dot-product attention, Dehghani et al.), z-loss regularization, and gradient clipping.
Understand Checkpointing and Rollback Strategies: automated anomaly detection, checkpoint frequency, saving optimizer states, and rolling back with modified data shuffle seeds.
Study Learning Rate Warmup and Decay: why linear warmup prevents destructive updates in randomly initialized representations, and comparing cosine vs WSD (Warmup-Stable-Decay) schedules.

modules.outcome: implement QK-Norm and z-loss regularization in a Transformer architecture and demonstrate suppression of attention logit explosion during training.

modules.name: Capstone: Compute-Optimal Pre-Training Experiment and Scaling Law Curve Fitting

objectives.text: Design an empirical pre-training experiment to fit Kaplan and Chinchilla scaling laws across a micro-cluster.
Construct a cleaned, deduplicated, and filtered training corpus with balanced domain mixing (code, mathematics, general prose).
Train a family of 5 decoder-only Transformer models spanning parameters from 10M to 150M across varied token allocations (10M to 1B tokens).
Log training loss, validation perplexity, gradient norms, and cumulative floating point operations (FLOPs) accurately using theoretical FLOP formulas: 6 * N * D per training step.
Fit parametric scaling law equations: L(N, D) = E + A / N^alpha + B / D^beta using non-linear curve fitting (SciPy optimize curve_fit).
Extract the optimal parameter-to-token ratio and compare empirical findings against Chinchilla predictions (alpha approx 0.34, beta approx 0.28).
Evaluate the downstream zero-shot capability of the models on standard language evaluation benchmarks to test whether loss scaling correlates with task performance.
Draft an academic research paper documenting the pre-training pipeline, dataset preparation, loss spike mitigation strategies, and scaling law exponent derivations.

modules.finalResult: a reproducible pre-training codebase, fitted scaling law power-law parameters, and academic paper analyzing empirical loss scaling dynamics.

completionOutcomes: Derive the theoretical floating point operations (FLOPs) required for forward and backward passes of a Transformer: 6 * N * D.
Explain the mathematical difference between Kaplan and Chinchilla scaling laws.
Derive the compute-optimal parameter-to-token allocation under a fixed compute budget constraint.
Explain why modern open-weight models are intentionally trained far past the Chinchilla compute-optimal frontier.
Implement MinHash and Locality-Sensitive Hashing (LSH) for large-scale text deduplication.
Train fastText quality classifiers to score web-scraped documents against high-quality reference corpora.
Explain the phenomenon of model collapse when recursively training on synthetic data.
Implement Byte-Pair Encoding (BPE) from scratch and inspect the vocabulary merge tree.
Identify tokenization failure modes affecting arithmetic, code indentation, and multilingual representations.
Analyze the structural causes of pre-training loss spikes and attention logit growth.
Implement QK-Norm and z-loss to ensure numerical stability during multi-billion parameter pre-training.
Formulate and execute a multi-model scaling law experiment and fit power-law coefficients.
Explain the Warmup-Stable-Decay (WSD) learning rate schedule and its advantages over standard cosine decay.

Progression: Scaling Laws & Chinchilla Optimality → Pre-Training Data Curation & Deduplication → Synthetic Data & Model Collapse → Tokenization Frontiers → Pre-Training Stability & Loss Spikes → Scaling Law Curve Fitting Capstone.

levels.title: Distributed ML Systems & High-Performance Training
levels.scope: master large-scale computational systems for deep learning research: modern GPU/accelerator architectures, 3D parallelism (tensor, pipeline, data), ZeRO and FSDP memory optimization, collective communication algorithms, and mixed-precision dynamics.

modules.name: GPU Microarchitecture, Memory Hierarchy & Roofline Modeling

objectives.text: Understand modern AI accelerator architectures: Streaming Multiprocessors (SMs), Tensor Cores, warp scheduling, and register file allocation.
Analyze the GPU memory hierarchy: registers, shared memory / L1 cache, L2 cache, and High Bandwidth Memory (HBM2e / HBM3e).
Master the Roofline Model: compute bound vs memory bandwidth bound regimes, operational arithmetic intensity (FLOPs per byte transferred).
Analyze hardware interconnects: NVLink bandwidth (up to 900 GB/s per GPU), NVSwitch topologies, PCIe Gen4/Gen5 constraints, and inter-node InfiniBand (HDR/NDR) fabrics.
Understand Triton and CUDA kernel programming conceptually: writing custom fused operators to avoid materializing intermediate activation tensors to global HBM.
Measure Model FLOPs Utilization (MFU) and Hardware FLOPs Utilization (HFU): calculating real hardware efficiency against theoretical peak specs.

modules.outcome: calculate the operational intensity of attention and linear layers, and measure MFU for a training run on a modern GPU.

modules.name: Distributed Parallelism: DP, DDP, TP, PP & Sequence Parallelism

objectives.text: Master Data Parallelism: DistributedDataParallel (DDP), gradient all-reduce synchronization, bucketed communication, and overlap of backward computation with communication.
Master Tensor Parallelism (Megatron-LM, Shoeybi et al.): intra-layer weight splitting across GPUs for ColumnParallelLinear and RowParallelLinear in attention and MLP blocks.
Analyze communications in Tensor Parallelism: Forward pass All-Gather / All-Reduce and Backward pass All-Reduce, and why TP requires ultra-high bandwidth NVLink interconnects.
Master Pipeline Parallelism (GPipe, PipeDream): partitioning network layers across stages, managing the pipeline bubble problem, and 1F1B (one-forward-one-backward) scheduling.
Analyze Sequence Parallelism (Korthikanti et al., DeepSpeed Ulysses, RingAttention): splitting the sequence dimension across GPUs to overcome single-device context limits.
Understand 3D Parallelism: combining Data Parallelism (DP), Tensor Parallelism (TP), and Pipeline Parallelism (PP) to train models exceeding 100 billion parameters.

modules.outcome: implement a manual 2-GPU Tensor Parallel linear layer in PyTorch using torch.distributed primitives (All-Reduce).

modules.name: Memory-Efficient Training: ZeRO & Fully Sharded Data Parallelism

objectives.text: Analyze the memory footprint of training a deep neural network:
Model parameters (4 bytes per parameter in FP32, 2 bytes in FP16/BF16).
Gradients (4 bytes in FP32 or 2 bytes in mixed precision).
Optimizer states (Adam stores FP32 master weights, momentum, and variance: 16 bytes per parameter).
Activations (scales with batch size, sequence length, layers, hidden dimension, and attention heads).
Activation checkpointing / gradient checkpointing: recomputing activations in backward pass to reduce memory footprint by 5-10x at the cost of a 30% compute overhead.
Temporary buffers and memory fragmentation.
Master Zero Redundancy Optimizer (ZeRO, Rajbhandari et al.):
ZeRO-Stage 1: sharding optimizer states across data-parallel ranks (4x memory reduction with zero communication overhead).
ZeRO-Stage 2: sharding optimizer states and gradients (further 2x reduction).
ZeRO-Stage 3: sharding optimizer states, gradients, and model parameters across all ranks (linear memory scaling with DP world size).
Master Fully Sharded Data Parallel (FSDP, PyTorch): native implementation of ZeRO-3, forward all-gather, backward all-gather, and reduce-scatter mechanics.

modules.outcome: compute the exact memory footprint of a 7B model under DDP vs ZeRO-1 vs ZeRO-3, and train an over-sized model on single-node GPUs using PyTorch FSDP.

modules.name: Collective Communications & Ring All-Reduce Algorithms

objectives.text: Understand collective communication primitives: Broadcast, Scatter, Gather, All-Gather, Reduce, Reduce-Scatter, and All-Reduce.
Analyze naive communication algorithms (parameter server, centralized hub) and their linear bandwidth bottlenecks O(N) with cluster size.
Master the Ring All-Reduce algorithm (Baidu, Gibiansky): dividing communication into Ring Reduce-Scatter followed by Ring All-Gather.
Derive Ring All-Reduce communication volume: 2 * ((N - 1) / N) * S bytes transferred per GPU, proving communication time is independent of the number of GPUs N.
Study Tree-based All-Reduce and Recursive Halving-Doubling algorithms for multi-node network topologies.
Analyze NCCL (NVIDIA Collective Communications Library): hierarchical ring algorithms routing intra-node traffic via NVLink and inter-node traffic via InfiniBand.

modules.outcome: implement Ring All-Reduce from scratch in Python using peer-to-peer point-to-point send/recv calls and verify correct gradient averaging.

modules.name: Low-Precision Representations: FP16, BF16, FP8 & Quantization Science

objectives.text: Analyze floating-point number formats: sign bit, exponent bits (dynamic range), and mantissa bits (precision).
Compare FP16 (5 exponent, 10 mantissa) and BF16 (8 exponent, 7 mantissa): why BF16 matches FP32 dynamic range and prevents underflow without loss scaling.
Master Mixed Precision Training (Micikevicius et al.): keeping FP32 master weights, casting forward/backward passes to FP16/BF16, and dynamic loss scaling.
Analyze FP8 Training (Micikevicius et al. 2022): E4M3 (higher precision for forward activations/weights) vs E5M2 (higher dynamic range for backward gradients) formats.
Study Post-Training Quantization (PTQ): INT8, INT4, weight-only quantization (AWQ, GPTQ), and activation outliers in LLMs (LLM.int8(), Dettmers et al.).
Explore Quantization-Aware Training (QAT): straight-through estimator (STE) and modeling quantization noise during forward passes.

modules.outcome: implement an automatic mixed-precision training loop using torch.cuda.amp with custom dynamic loss scaling and gradient clipping.

modules.name: Capstone: Scale a Multi-Billion Parameter Model using FSDP with Profiling & MFU Analysis

objectives.text: Configure a distributed training pipeline to train a multi-billion parameter foundation model across multiple GPUs using PyTorch Fully Sharded Data Parallel (FSDP).
Implement backward activation checkpointing and CPU offloading to maximize permissible batch size and context window length.
Configure FSDP sharding strategy (FULL_SHARD vs SHARD_GRAD_OP) and auto-wrap policy targeting custom Transformer decoder layers.
Implement mixed precision training using BF16 / FP16 with native PyTorch torch.distributed operations.
Profile execution using PyTorch Profiler and NVIDIA Nsight Systems: inspect SM utilization, memory allocations, communication vs computation overlap, and kernel execution timelines.
Calculate theoretical peak FLOPs for the hardware cluster and compute the empirical Model FLOPs Utilization (MFU) of the training run.

Conduct an ablation study measuring training throughput (tokens per second) and memory savings across: (1) standard DDP, (2) FSDP without activation checkpointing, and (3) FSDP with activation checkpointing and operator fusion.
Draft a systems research report detailing the scaling efficiency, communication overhead, MFU benchmarks, and memory allocation profiles.

modules.finalResult: a production-grade distributed training codebase, complete with profiling traces and a systems paper evaluating high-performance scaling efficiency.

completionOutcomes: Apply the Roofline model to determine whether a neural network layer is compute-bound or memory-bound.
Calculate Model FLOPs Utilization (MFU) to measure empirical training efficiency on GPUs.
Derive the communication and computational mechanics of Megatron-LM Tensor Parallelism.
Explain the pipeline bubble problem in Pipeline Parallelism and how 1F1B scheduling mitigates idle time.
Calculate the exact memory breakdown of model weights, gradients, optimizer states, and activations.
Explain the three stages of the Zero Redundancy Optimizer (ZeRO) and their impact on memory footprint.
Configure PyTorch Fully Sharded Data Parallel (FSDP) for multi-billion parameter model training.
Derive the Ring All-Reduce communication complexity and prove its independence from the number of devices.
Explain the architectural difference between FP16 and BF16 and why BF16 prevents underflow.
Implement automatic mixed precision training with dynamic loss scaling.
Use PyTorch Profiler and NVIDIA Nsight to identify communication bottlenecks and memory fragmentation.
Analyze activation outliers and explain their impact on INT8/INT4 post-training quantization.

Progression: GPU Microarchitecture & Roofline Modeling → 3D Parallelism (DP, TP, PP, SP) → ZeRO & FSDP Memory Optimization → Collective Communications & Ring All-Reduce → Low-Precision FP8/BF16 Science → Distributed Scaling Capstone.

levels.title: Generative Modeling: VAEs, GANs & Diffusion Theory
levels.scope: explore the theoretical and mathematical foundations of deep generative modeling: variational inference, generative adversarial networks, score-based models, stochastic differential equations (SDEs), and continuous-time flow matching.

modules.name: Variational Autoencoders & The Evidence Lower Bound

objectives.text: Formulate generative modeling as estimating the true data distribution p_data(x) and sampling novel instances x ~ p_theta(x).
Analyze the intractability of marginal likelihood p_theta(x) = \int p_theta(x, z) dz in high-dimensional latent variable models.
Derive the Evidence Lower Bound (ELBO) mathematically using Jensen's inequality: log p_theta(x) >= E_q[log p_theta(x|z)] - D_KL(q_phi(z|x) || p(z)).
Decompose ELBO into reconstruction loss and latent KL divergence regularization against a standard isotropic Gaussian prior N(0, I).
Master the Reparameterization Trick (Kingma & Welling): z = mu_phi(x) + sigma_phi(x) \odot epsilon, where epsilon ~ N(0, I), enabling backpropagation through stochastic nodes.
Analyze posterior collapse: when the decoder ignores latent variables z and acts as an unconditional autoregressive model.
Explore Hierarchical and Vector-Quantized VAEs (VQ-VAE, Van den Oord et al.): discrete latent representations and codebook learning without posterior collapse.

modules.outcome: derive the analytical KL divergence between two multivariate Gaussian distributions and implement a VAE with the reparameterization trick in PyTorch.

modules.name: Generative Adversarial Networks & Minimax Game Theory

objectives.text: Formulate GANs as a two-player zero-sum minimax game: min_G max_D V(D, G) = E_{x~p_data}[log D(x)] + E_{z~p_z}[log(1 - D(G(z)))].
Prove mathematically that the optimal discriminator for any fixed generator G is D^*(x) = p_data(x) / (p_data(x) + p_g(x)).
Prove that substituting D^*(x) into the minimax objective reduces the generator loss to the Jensen-Shannon Divergence (JSD): 2 * JSD(p_data || p_g) - 2 * log(2).
Analyze GAN Training Pathologies: vanishing gradients with saturated discriminators, non-convergence in non-convex game dynamics, and Mode Collapse.
Study Wasserstein GANs (WGAN, Arjovsky et al.): using Earth Mover's Distance (Kantorovich-Rubinstein duality), 1-Lipschitz continuity constraints, and Gradient Penalty (WGAN-GP).

modules.outcome: prove that the global minimum of the minimax GAN objective occurs if and only if p_g = p_data, and implement WGAN with gradient penalty.

modules.name: Score-Based Generative Modeling & Denoising Diffusion (DDPM)

objectives.text: Understand Score Matching (Hyvarinen): modeling the score function of data distribution: s_theta(x) = \nabla_x log p(x) without computing intractable partition functions Z.
Analyze Langevin Dynamics: sampling from a distribution using its score function via gradient ascent with Gaussian noise perturbations.
Master Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models (DDPM, Sohl-Dickstein et al., Ho et al.): forward noising process q(x_t|x_{t-1}) and reverse denoising process p_theta(x_{t-1}|x_t).
Derive the closed-form forward marginal q(x_t|x_0) = N(x_t; sqrt(alpha_bar_t) * x_0, (1 - alpha_bar_t) * I) using Gaussian reproductive properties.
Derive the simplified DDPM training objective: predicting the injected Gaussian noise epsilon_theta(x_t, t) using L2 mean squared error loss ||epsilon - epsilon_theta(x_t, t)||^2.
Analyze Noise Schedules: linear, cosine (Nichol & Dhariwal), and continuous schedules, and their impact on sample quality and signal-to-noise ratio (SNR).

modules.outcome: derive the closed-form forward sampling equation q(x_t|x_0) and implement an end-to-end DDPM training and sampling loop in PyTorch.

modules.name: Continuous SDEs & Probability Flow ODEs

objectives.text: Formulate the continuous-time generalization of diffusion models using Stochastic Differential Equations (Score-based SDEs, Song et al. 2020).
Analyze Forward Itô SDEs: dx = f(x, t) dt + g(t) dw, transforming complex data distributions into isotropic Gaussian noise.
Master Anderson's Reverse-Time SDE Theorem: dx = [f(x, t) - g(t)^2 * \nabla_x log p_t(x)] dt + g(t) dw_bar, proving reversal is an SDE guided by the score function.
Derive the Probability Flow ODE: deterministic ordinary differential equation sharing the exact same marginal probability trajectories p_t(x) as the reverse SDE.

Understand the benefits of the Probability Flow ODE: deterministic sampling, fast numerical ODE solvers (RK4, Euler), exact likelihood computation via instantaneous change of variables, and latent space inversion.
Analyze Accelerated Samplers: DDIM (Denoising Diffusion Implicit Models, Song et al.), DPM-Solver (Lu et al.), reducing sampling steps from 1000 down to 15-20 steps.

modules.outcome: formulate the probability flow ODE for a variance-preserving (VP) SDE and implement a DDIM deterministic sampler in PyTorch.

modules.name: Flow Matching & Optimal Transport in Latent Spaces

objectives.text: Understand Continuous Normalizing Flows (CNFs): learning time-dependent vector fields v_t(x) that transport a simple base distribution (e.g. standard Gaussian) to a target data distribution.
Analyze the intractability of standard CNF maximum likelihood: requiring expensive ODE integration during every training step.
Master Flow Matching (Lipman et al., Albergo & Vanden-Eijnden): training neural vector fields directly on conditional probability paths via simple regression without ODE simulation.

Analyze Optimal Transport Flow Matching (OT-FM): straight-line displacement paths between noise x_0 and data x_1: x_t = (1 - t) * x_0 + t * x_1 with constant target velocity u_t(x|x_1, x_0) = x_1 - x_0.
Prove that straight-line probability trajectories minimize kinetic energy, leading to significantly simpler ODE trajectories that can be solved in as few as 4-8 integration steps.

Examine Latent Diffusion Models (LDM / Stable Diffusion, Rombach et al.): compressing high-dimensional images into lower-dimensional latent spaces using a pre-trained VAE before applying diffusion / flow matching.
Study Classifier-Free Guidance (CFG, Ho & Salimans): interpolating between unconditional and conditional vector fields to dramatically improve generation fidelity and prompt adherence.

modules.outcome: implement Optimal Transport Flow Matching from scratch and train a flow model on 2D synthetic distributions and images with straight-line trajectories.

modules.name: Capstone: Implement a Continuous Flow Matching Model from Mathematical First Principles

objectives.text: Build and train a continuous-time Flow Matching generative model from mathematical scratch on a dataset of images or complex scientific multi-modal trajectories.
Implement the Optimal Transport interpolation path: x_t = (1 - (1 - sigma_min) * t) * x_0 + t * x_1, and derive the ground-truth target velocity field u_t(x_t|x_0, x_1).
Implement a U-Net or Diffusion Transformer (DiT, Peebles & Xie) architecture to parameterize the time-dependent velocity field v_theta(x, t).
Integrate adaptive layer normalization (AdaLN) conditioning on timestep t and class / text embeddings.
Train the model by regressing v_theta(x_t, t) onto target velocity u_t using simple mean squared error loss with zero ODE simulation during training.
Implement numerical ODE integration samplers (Euler method, Midpoint method, and Runge-Kutta 4th order RK4) to generate samples at inference time.
Implement Classifier-Free Guidance (CFG) within the vector field sampling loop with guidance scale parameter w.
Evaluate generation quality quantitatively: compute Fréchet Inception Distance (FID) and measure integration step requirements (evaluating performance at 4, 10, 25, and 50 steps).
Draft an academic research paper comparing Flow Matching against DDPM in terms of training stability, trajectory curvature, and sample generation speed.

modules.finalResult: a verified Flow Matching generative model codebase, sampling notebook, and academic paper dissecting optimal transport trajectories.

completionOutcomes: Derive the Evidence Lower Bound (ELBO) mathematically using Jensen's inequality.
Explain why the reparameterization trick enables gradient backpropagation through stochastic latent nodes.
Prove that the global optimum of the original GAN objective is achieved when the generator distribution equals the data distribution.
Explain mode collapse in GANs and how Wasserstein distance (WGAN-GP) improves training stability.
Derive the closed-form forward sampling formula q(x_t|x_0) for Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models (DDPM).
Explain the difference between score matching and likelihood-based generative modeling.
Formulate diffusion models as continuous Stochastic Differential Equations (SDEs) and reverse-time SDEs.
Derive the Probability Flow ODE and explain how it enables deterministic sampling and exact likelihood computation.
Explain the mathematical formulation of Flow Matching and why it avoids ODE simulation during training.
Prove that Optimal Transport Flow Matching produces straight-line paths with minimal kinetic energy.
Implement Classifier-Free Guidance (CFG) and explain its effect on sample fidelity and diversity.
Build a Diffusion Transformer (DiT) architecture with adaptive layer normalization conditioning.
Evaluate generative models using Fréchet Inception Distance (FID) and Inception Score (IS).

Progression: VAEs & ELBO Foundations → GANs & Wasserstein Minimax → DDPM & Score Matching → Continuous SDEs & Probability Flow ODEs → Flow Matching & Optimal Transport → Continuous Flow Matching Capstone.

levels.title: Multimodal & Cross-Modal Representation Research
levels.scope: investigate representation learning across perceptual modalities: contrastive vision-language alignment, visual tokenization, autoregressive multimodal foundation architectures, cross-attention fusion, speech representations, and video latent dynamics.

modules.name: Contrastive Vision-Language Alignment: CLIP & SigLIP

objectives.text: Understand multimodal alignment: mapping heterogeneous data modalities (images and text) into a shared semantic latent space.
Master CLIP (Contrastive Language-Image Pre-Training, Radford et al.): dual-encoder architecture (Vision Transformer image encoder + Transformer text encoder).
Analyze the symmetric InfoNCE loss function: maximizing cosine similarity of matched image-text pairs along the diagonal while penalizing off-diagonal pairs.
Study Zero-Shot Classification via CLIP: constructing prompt templates ("a photo of a {label}"), encoding candidate text labels, and computing cosine classification probabilities.
Master SigLIP (Sigmoid Loss for Language Image Pre-Training, Zhai et al.): replacing the global Softmax normalization with pairwise sigmoid loss.
Analyze the benefits of SigLIP: eliminating the global all-gather communication bottleneck across distributed GPUs, enabling larger batch sizes and stable scaling.
Examine Modality Gap (Liang et al.): the geometric phenomenon where image embeddings and text embeddings occupy completely disjoint cones in latent space.

modules.outcome: derive SigLIP loss mathematically and train a dual-encoder vision-language model with contrastive alignment on image-text pairs.

modules.name: Visual Tokenization & Discrete Representation Learning

objectives.text: Understand the difference between continuous visual representations (patches) and discrete visual tokens.
Master the Vision Transformer (ViT, Dosovitskiy et al.): image patch extraction (e.g. 16x16 pixels), linear patch projection, learnable class token [CLS], and 2D positional encodings.

Study Vector-Quantized Variational Autoencoders (VQ-VAE, Van den Oord et al.): continuous encoder, discrete codebook discretization via nearest-neighbor vector quantization, and straight-through estimator (STE).
Master VQ-GAN (Esser et al.): augmenting VQ-VAE with adversarial perceptual loss and patch-based discriminator to generate crisp high-frequency textures without blurriness.
Explore Continuous Patch Tokenization vs Discrete Tokens: analyzing why modern Vision-Language Models (VLMs) favor continuous patch representations over discrete codebooks.
Analyze High-Resolution Image Processing: dynamic tiling, patch cropping, and spatial aspect-ratio preserving grids in modern Large Multimodal Models (LMMs).

modules.outcome: implement a discrete vector quantization layer with Straight-Through Estimator (STE) gradient copying in PyTorch.

modules.name: Vision-Language Foundation Models & Multimodal Adapters

objectives.text: Analyze the architectural taxonomy of modern Vision-Language Models:
Dual-encoder alignment (CLIP style) versus unified autoregressive multimodal generation (LLaVA, Flamingo, PaLM-E).
Linear Projections and Multi-Layer Perceptrons (MLP adapters, LLaVA, Liu et al.): projecting visual patch tokens directly into the LLM text token embedding space.
Cross-Attention Architectures (Flamingo, Alayrac et al.): gated cross-attention layers interleaved within frozen language model Transformer blocks.
Resamplers and Bottlenecks (Q-Former in BLIP-2, Perceiver Resampler): using fixed-size query tokens to compress variable-length visual patches into a fixed number of tokens.
Stage 1: Pre-training for feature alignment on massive image-caption pairs (training only the projection adapter while keeping vision encoder and LLM frozen).
Stage 2: Visual Instruction Tuning (fine-tuning the projection adapter and LLM on detailed multi-turn visual conversations, visual reasoning, and QA).
Analyze Object Hallucination in LMMs: models claiming non-existent objects exist in images due to language prior bias overpowering visual features (POPE benchmark).
Study Spatial Grounding and Coordinate Modeling: bounding box prediction ([x_min, y_min, x_max, y_max] normalized coordinates), visual pointing, and region-of-interest tokens.

modules.outcome: implement an MLP projection adapter connecting a pre-trained Vision Transformer to an open-weight language model and perform end-to-end forward generation.

modules.name: Audio, Speech & Continuous Representation Research

objectives.text: Understand acoustic representations: audio waveforms, Fourier transforms, Short-Time Fourier Transform (STFT), and Mel-frequency spectrograms.
Study Self-Supervised Speech Representation: wav2vec 2.0 (Baevski et al.), masked acoustic modeling, and contrastive loss over quantized latent representations.
Master Whisper (Radford et al.): weakly supervised encoder-decoder Transformer trained on 680,000 hours of multilingual audio for robust speech-to-text transcription.
Analyze Continuous Acoustic Tokenization: SoundStream and EnCodec (Défossez et al.), Residual Vector Quantization (RVQ), and neural audio codecs.
Explore Speech-Language Foundation Models: unified tokenization of speech and text, zero-shot voice cloning, and real-time duplex speech generation.

modules.outcome: implement a Mel-spectrogram feature extractor and inspect phonetic representations extracted from intermediate layers of a pre-trained speech model.

modules.name: Video Representation Learning & Spatiotemporal Dynamics

objectives.text: Understand the spatiotemporal challenges of video modeling: adding the temporal dimension T expands data dimensionality and computational complexity quadratically.

Study Spatiotemporal Attention: factorized space-time attention (TimeSformer, Bertasius et al., Video Swin Transformer) separating spatial attention within frames from temporal attention across frames.
Analyze 3D VAEs and Video Diffusion: inflating 2D spatial convolutions and attention layers to 3D spatiotemporal blocks for video generation (Sora, VideoLDM).
Study Causal Video Tokenization: maintaining temporal causality so future frames cannot leak information into past frame token representations.
Analyze Long-Form Video Understanding: memory caching, temporal pooling, and sparse sampling techniques to reason over hour-long video contexts.

modules.outcome: implement factorized space-time self-attention in PyTorch and verify computational memory savings compared to full joint space-time attention.

modules.name: Capstone: Train a Vision-Language Adapter (LLaVA-Style) with Visual Grounding and Hallucination Probing

objectives.text: Build an end-to-end Large Multimodal Model (LMM) pipeline by training a vision-language projection adapter connecting a frozen Vision Transformer (CLIP-ViT) to a frozen decoder language model.
Implement a two-layer MLP projection adapter with GELU non-linearity to align visual patch tokens with the language model embedding dimension.
Curate an image-instruction dataset (e.g. LLaVA-Instruct subset or ChartQA/VQA subset) with conversational visual question answering examples.
Execute Stage 1 Feature Alignment: train the projection adapter on image-caption pairs using autoregressive language modeling loss with frozen vision and LLM weights.
Execute Stage 2 Visual Instruction Tuning: fine-tune the adapter and top Transformer layers of the LLM on multimodal instruction data.

Conduct an empirical study on Multimodal Object Hallucination using the POPE (Polling-based Object Probing Evaluation) benchmark: measure precision, recall, and F1 across random, popular, and adversarial negative object questions.
Implement attention rollout or cross-modal attention attribution to visualize which visual image patches the language model attends to when generating factual responses.
Draft an academic research paper documenting the architecture, multimodal alignment loss dynamics, hallucination benchmark results, and attention heatmaps.

modules.finalResult: a working vision-language foundation model checkpoint, training codebase, and research paper analyzing multimodal alignment and hallucination dynamics.

completionOutcomes: Formulate the contrastive vision-language alignment objective of CLIP.
Derive SigLIP loss and explain how pairwise sigmoid loss eliminates all-gather communication bottlenecks.
Explain the Modality Gap phenomenon in joint multimodal representation spaces.
Implement the Vision Transformer (ViT) patch extraction and linear projection mechanics.
Explain the Vector-Quantized VAE (VQ-VAE) codebook mechanism and the Straight-Through Estimator.
Contrast linear projection adapters (LLaVA style) with cross-attention architectures (Flamingo style).
Design a two-stage training curriculum for Large Multimodal Models (alignment followed by instruction tuning).
Explain the root causes of visual object hallucination in vision-language models.
Formulate spatial grounding using normalized coordinate tokens in language models.
Transform raw audio waveforms into Mel-spectrograms and explain the wav2vec 2.0 self-supervised objective.
Explain Residual Vector Quantization (RVQ) used in modern neural audio codecs.
Implement factorized spatiotemporal attention for video understanding.
Evaluate vision-language models on visual reasoning and object hallucination benchmarks (POPE, VQA).

Progression: Contrastive Multimodal Alignment (CLIP/SigLIP) → Visual Tokenization & ViT → Large Multimodal Models (LLaVA/Flamingo) → Speech & Audio Representations → Video Spatiotemporal Dynamics → Vision-Language Adapter Capstone.

levels.title: Post-Training, Parameter-Efficient Tuning & Continual Learning
levels.scope: investigate scientific techniques for adapting and steering foundation models: spectral theory of Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA/DoRA), representation collapse, catastrophic forgetting, continual learning dynamics, and model merging.

modules.name: Theory of Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT)

objectives.text: Understand the computational and storage impracticality of full parameter fine-tuning for massive foundation models across specialized downstream domains.
Analyze the Intrinsic Dimensionality of Deep Models (Aghajanyan et al.): proving that the parameter updates required for downstream tasks occupy a very low-dimensional intrinsic subspace.
Master Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA, Hu et al.): reparameterizing weight updates as Delta W = B * A * (alpha / r), where B \in R^{d x r}, A \in R^{r x k}, and rank r << min(d, k).
Analyze LoRA Initialization: initializing A with Gaussian random noise and B with zeros so that Delta W = 0 at the start of training, preserving exact base model behavior.

Master Weight-Decomposed Low-Rank Adaptation (DoRA, Liu et al.): decomposing weights into magnitude and directional components W = m * (V + Delta V) / ||V + Delta V||_F to bridge the performance gap with full fine-tuning.
Explore Prefix Tuning and Prompt Tuning: prepending learnable continuous virtual tokens to key and value matrices in attention layers.

modules.outcome: derive LoRA mathematically, prove that rank r updates preserve parameter gradients in a low-dimensional manifold, and implement custom LoRA layers from scratch.

modules.name: Spectral Analysis of LoRA & Subspace Geometry

objectives.text: Analyze the Singular Value Decomposition (SVD) of fine-tuned weight differences: Delta W = U \Sigma V^T and analyze the rapid decay of singular values.
Study Subspace Similarity: computing Grassmannian distance and principal angles between the subspaces spanned by LoRA matrices and full parameter update matrices.
Investigate Rank Over-Allocation: what happens when rank r is chosen larger than the true intrinsic rank of the downstream adaptation task?
Analyze which Transformer modules benefit most from low-rank adaptation: query/key/value attention projections versus MLP feedforward expansions.
Study QLoRA (Dettmers et al.): NormalFloat4 (NF4) data type, Double Quantization (DQ), and Paged Optimizers to enable fine-tuning 70B models on single consumer GPUs.

modules.outcome: compute the singular value spectrum of LoRA matrices across training checkpoints to empirically observe rank saturation and subspace alignment.

modules.name: Catastrophic Forgetting & Continual Learning Dynamics

objectives.text: Define Catastrophic Forgetting (McCloskey & Cohen): the severe degradation of previously learned capabilities when a neural network is fine-tuned sequentially on new domains.
Analyze the Stability-Plasticity Dilemma: balancing the acquisition of new knowledge (plasticity) against the retention of prior knowledge (stability).
Study Continual Learning Methodologies:
Elastic Weight Consolidation (EWC, Kirkpatrick et al.): penalizing changes to parameters critical to past tasks using the diagonal of the empirical Fisher Information Matrix.
Synaptic Intelligence and memory-aware synapses: tracking path integrals of parameter importance online during training.
Experience Replay: storing a small buffer of exemplar data from earlier tasks and mixing them into current training batches.
Generative Replay: using a generative model to produce synthetic samples of earlier tasks to interleave during adaptation.
Progressive Neural Networks and modular parameter allocation: freezing old task sub-networks and adding new modules for novel tasks.

modules.outcome: derive Elastic Weight Consolidation (EWC) mathematically using Laplace approximation of the posterior distribution and implement EWC loss in PyTorch.

modules.name: Model Merging, Weight Averaging & Task Arithmetic

objectives.text: Understand Model Merging: combining multiple independently fine-tuned models into a single multi-task model without access to original training data or additional gradient updates.
Study Linear Weight Averaging: Stochastic Weight Averaging (SWA, Izmailov et al.) and Model Soups (Wortsman et al.) averaging checkpoints in flat loss basins.

Master Task Arithmetic (Ilharco et al.): treating fine-tuned models as task vectors tau_t = W_fine-tuned - W_base, enabling task addition (multi-task combination) and task subtraction (unlearning concepts).
Analyze Interference and Parameter Clash: when task vectors have conflicting gradient directions in overlapping parameter dimensions.
Study Advanced Merging Algorithms:
TIES-Merging (Yadav et al.): Trimming redundant small values, Resolving sign conflicts, and Merging aligned parameters.
DARE (Drop And REscale, Yu et al.): extreme random sparsification of task vectors followed by rescaling to prevent representation collapse.
Spherical Linear Interpolation (SLERP): interpolating weights along the geodesic of high-dimensional spheres rather than linear Euclidean interpolation.

modules.outcome: implement Task Vector addition and TIES-Merging in Python, evaluating multi-task accuracy retention across independently fine-tuned checkpoints.

modules.name: Representation Drift & Mechanistic Effects of Post-Training

objectives.text: Investigate Representation Drift: analyzing how internal latent representations shift during fine-tuning, instruction tuning, and alignment.

Study the "Surface Form Hypothesis" (Zhou et al., LIMA): hypothesis that pre-training learns virtually all factual knowledge and reasoning, while post-training primarily learns style, formatting, and interactive behavior.
Measure Representation Drift using Centered Kernel Alignment (CKA) and Procrustes distance across pre-trained and fine-tuned layer activations.
Analyze Weight Disentanglement: identifying whether post-training modifies core attention mechanisms or isolated late-layer projections.
Examine Unlearning and Concept Erasure in Fine-Tuned Models: representation editing to remove copyrighted text, hazardous chemical knowledge, or personally identifiable information (PII).

modules.outcome: measure the layer-wise CKA similarity between base and instruction-tuned model checkpoints to empirically test the Surface Form Hypothesis.

modules.name: Capstone: Empirical Study of Representation Drift and Subspace Conservation in LoRA vs Full Fine-Tuning

objectives.text: Design an empirical research experiment comparing parameter-efficient adaptation (LoRA) against full parameter fine-tuning on a specialized scientific or reasoning task.
Fine-tune identical base foundation models using: (1) Full parameter fine-tuning, (2) LoRA with low rank (r=4), (3) LoRA with high rank (r=64), and (4) DoRA.
Track training dynamics, validation loss, and task accuracy over identical training epochs.
Evaluate Catastrophic Forgetting: measure accuracy drops on standard general-domain language benchmarks (MMLU, GSM8K, ARC) before and after domain adaptation.

Compute Singular Value Decomposition (SVD) of weight update matrices Delta W for full fine-tuning and compare principal subspace overlap against the learned LoRA matrices using Grassmannian distance metrics.
Perform Centered Kernel Alignment (CKA) across all Transformer layers to map exact representation drift across the network depth.
Conduct Task Vector arithmetic: test whether subtracting the fine-tuned task vector cleanly reverses domain adaptation without damaging pre-trained general knowledge.
Draft an academic research paper presenting singular value spectra, CKA drift heatmaps, forgetting benchmarks, and theoretical analysis of low-rank subspace conservation.

modules.finalResult: a reproducible PEFT research benchmark codebase, evaluation notebook, and academic paper evaluating representation drift and forgetting dynamics.

completionOutcomes: Explain the Intrinsic Dimensionality hypothesis of deep neural network fine-tuning.
Derive the Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) reparameterization Delta W = B * A.
Explain the initialization scheme of LoRA and why it guarantees identity mapping at step zero.
Formulate DoRA (Weight-Decomposed LoRA) and explain how magnitude-direction decoupling improves expressivity.
Analyze the singular value spectrum of weight updates using Singular Value Decomposition (SVD).
Explain the mechanics of QLoRA: NormalFloat4 (NF4) quantization, Double Quantization, and Paged Optimizers.
Define catastrophic forgetting and state the stability-plasticity dilemma.
Derive Elastic Weight Consolidation (EWC) using the Fisher Information Matrix and Laplace approximation.
Explain the mechanics of Task Vector arithmetic: task addition, task subtraction, and unlearning.
Implement TIES-Merging and DARE to resolve parameter sign conflicts when merging multi-task models.
Explain the Surface Form Hypothesis and its implications for instruction fine-tuning datasets.
Measure representation drift across fine-tuning checkpoints using Centered Kernel Alignment (CKA).
Evaluate the trade-off between domain specialization and general-purpose knowledge retention.

Progression: Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning & LoRA → Spectral Analysis & Subspace Geometry → Catastrophic Forgetting & Continual Learning → Model Merging & Task Arithmetic → Representation Drift Science → LoRA vs Full Tuning Capstone.

modules.name: Architectural Benchmark: Sub-Quadratic State Space vs Attention Hybrid

objectives.text: Design, implement, and benchmark a hybrid architecture combining local self-attention with Mamba selective state space layers.
Evaluate long-context associative recall on needle-in-a-haystack synthetic probes and standard language modeling benchmarks.

modules.name: Mechanistic Dissection of In-Context Learning Circuits

modules.name: Continuous Optimal Transport Flow Matching on Complex Manifolds

objectives.text: Train a continuous-time Flow Matching generative model with optimal transport displacement paths on scientific dynamical systems or image datasets.
Implement adaptive layer normalization conditioning and a Diffusion Transformer (DiT) velocity backbone.
Compare ODE integration trajectories and sample quality against standard Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models (DDPM) across 4, 10, and 50 sampling steps.

modules.name: Robust Preference Optimization with Spectral SVD Regularization
